descriptions.github:5707633705: Context Mathlib's linters catch unused arguments, statements stated less generally than they could be, and duplicate declarations. Tengoku has the vacuity check and the axiom check but no duplicate or generality checks, and statements are accepted at the gate and promotion as long as they compile. What is wanted A design and a prototype for checks on records entering staging or trusted: - unused hypotheses and variables in a statement; - generality : a statement that is a special case of one already present; - duplication : the same statement under two names, found at kernel level (up to definitional unfolding and renaming of bound variables), not by text. Start by running such checks over the existing data and reporting how many records each would flag, with examples, before proposing any gate rule. Include how often each check would be wrong. Done when A report with counts and…
descriptions.github:5707633447: Context Tengoku's documentation, the README, and the pages on competemath.com describe the project in different words and make different claims. A draft of the wording to converge on, and an audit of the differences, is in the sandbox draft PR ( messaging-draft.md , consistency-audit-draft.md ). What is wanted After the drafts are settled, apply them across README.md and docs/ , and check for: - Leak described as tooling and a harness for agent-driven proving (search, proof states, verification over MCP) that any MCP-capable system can use, not as a prover; - Tengoku and Leak described as parts of one service, with Leak as the intended interface; - claims that cannot be backed (for example that the system prevents theft or misattribution of work) removed or reworded to what the checks actually do; - the same terms everywhere (tier names, "source" versus "library"); - spelling and…
descriptions.github:5707633187: Context CONTRIBUTING.md is complete but long. New contributors ask what to do first. What is wanted A one-page cheat sheet linked from CONTRIBUTING.md : - the four things you can contribute (a theorem, a project, a goal, a fix) and where each goes; - the PR classes ( docs/pr-classes.md ) in one table, with what each one is checked for; - the commands to run before you push (the pre-commit hooks, the unit tests, the gate scripts against origin/main ; see CONTRIBUTING.md ); - three suggested starting points, for example opening a PR that adds a goal to GOALS.md (see docs/goals.md ), fixing a documentation issue labelled good first issue , or reporting a record that looks wrong. Done when A new contributor can open a first PR using only this page, which another person confirms by following it. Difficulty: easy.
descriptions.github:5707632989: Context Links to the repository on social media and chat show GitHub's default card. A proper 1280×640 px preview image helps people recognise the project. What is wanted A PNG (under 1 MB, 1280×640) using the logo ( logo.png ) and the name "Tengoku (天国)", readable at thumbnail size, in a light and a dark variant if you like. Add the source file under docs/img/ . A maintainer sets it in the repository settings. Done when The image is merged in docs/img/ and renders well when previewed at small size. Difficulty: easy. Design, no code.
descriptions.github:5707632717: Context The v1.0.0 dataset is a gzipped JSONL release on GitHub with a Zenodo DOI. Hugging Face is where many people look for datasets. What is wanted - A dataset card from the data card in docs/ (fields, contents, known problems, licences, how to cite the DOI). - A conversion to a format the Hugging Face datasets library loads without custom code (Parquet or JSONL, with a schema), and a script that produces it from the release file. - A short loader example. A maintainer will do the upload under the project account; please prepare the files and the card. Done when datasets.load dataset works on the prepared files, the card's counts match the release, and the card says plainly which records are known to be wrong. Difficulty: medium.
descriptions.github:5707632478: Context Tengoku holds hundreds of thousands of theorems from public projects. A prover given access to it can score well on a benchmark whose problems or solutions are already in it. Anyone benchmarking against Tengoku needs to know the overlap before they start. What is wanted A script that takes a file of benchmark statements (a Lean file, or a JSONL of names and statements) and reports, for each, whether Tengoku already holds it: by exact name, by identical statement after normalisation, and by near-match (for example identical up to renaming of bound variables). Output a table and a summary count. Done when It runs on a small sample benchmark, is tested on cases of each kind, and is documented in docs/ . Difficulty: medium. Python; the search API at or the data files can be used.
descriptions.github:5707631864: Context data/stats.json was last generated on and is not refreshed by a promotion. The README badge, the website's counters and several documents read it, so the numbers they show are out of date. Counts differ between the files that state them (trusted, staging and tentative totals; counts per library). What is wanted 1. Regenerate data/stats.json on a schedule and after every promotion, through a bot PR or a workflow that follows the repository's rules (every change goes through the PR gate). 2. Generate one table of the key numbers (tentative, staging and trusted totals, and per library) from the same data, so every document can link to it instead of retyping numbers. A draft generator, scripts/coverage table.py , exists in the sandbox draft PR. Done when The numbers in stats.json match a fresh count of data/ , a test fails if they drift, and the table is regenerated with them…
descriptions.github:5707631509: Context The rule is that nothing trusted may be relocated or removed except by tombstoning. append only.py stops edits and deletions of data lines, but a trusted name could still move to another file or module, and a promotion could reshuffle where records live. What is wanted A check that, for every PR, the set of trusted names only grows or is tombstoned: no trusted name disappears from data/trusted/ or the generated modules without a tombstone line, and none changes file or module. List the legitimate exceptions (promotion of staging to trusted, the bot's regeneration) and keep them working. Done when Tests in scripts/ci/tests/ cover a move, a silent removal, a tombstone and a promotion; the check runs in pr-gate . It is proved in tengoku-sandbox first (see scripts/ci/campaign/README.md ). Difficulty: hard. Touches the gate; please talk to a maintainer before starting.
descriptions.github:5707631260: Context Records are append-only and live for years, but the formats for names, ids, Author: lines and credit corrections have changed and will change again. A reader of an old record should be able to find the format it was written in. What is wanted A docs/formats/ directory with one short file per format and per version: what the field looks like, when the version started (commit or date), what changed. Start from schemas/record.schema.json , CONTRIBUTING.md and git log on those files. Done when Every field in the record schema has a page or section, with its current rule and its history, and CONTRIBUTING.md links to it. Difficulty: easy. Reading and writing; no Lean needed.
descriptions.github:5707631013: Context A credit says who proved a result, but not when it was contributed. A date makes the order of discovery checkable and helps resolve disputes. What is wanted Decide and implement where the date lives (a field on the record, or part of the Author: line), keeping every rule that already holds: - data files are append-only, so existing records cannot be rewritten; the change must apply to new records and say what old records show; - credit lines are validated by scripts/ci/validate records.py and protected by scripts/ci/credits.py ; both need updating together; - the field goes in schemas/record.schema.json . Please propose the format here before writing code. Changes to the gate are tried in…
descriptions.github:5707630582: Context Credit is carried by an Author: line and a source link on each record. Today the gate checks that the line exists and is not removed. A wrong author line, added deliberately or by mistake, passes. We should not claim more than this, and we should look at what else can be checked. What is wanted 1. A short write-up of the attacks and mistakes the current checks stop and those they do not (for example: a copied theorem submitted under another name, a missing or wrong source link, a headline theorem re-submitted as new, an AI-generated paraphrase of an existing proof). 2. A design proposal (an issue comment or a document, not code yet) for additional checks, each with its false-positive risk: similarity of a new record to existing records and to its claimed source at the pinned commit, mismatch between the author line and the source's own authors, flagged near-duplicates of…
descriptions.github:5707630364: Context Tawatur is a proposed optional status beyond trusted . The idea comes from hadith studies, where a report transmitted by enough independent chains is treated as certain because independent errors are very unlikely to coincide. For a theorem, the proposal is that it has three independent proofs , with independence meaning the proofs' dependencies are pairwise disjoint. The concept is not finalised . This issue is for deciding what it should mean and whether it is worth having. Nothing about it is implemented, and nothing in the documentation should claim it is. Questions to answer 1. What does "independent" mean? Every Lean proof rests on the kernel, the core library and usually Mathlib, so strict disjointness is impossible. Options include: disjoint sets of non-core declarations; disjoint sets of the project's own declarations; different proof strategies on a shared base; proofs…
descriptions.github:5707630088: Context The entailment check (translated statement must imply the original) is meant to catch translations that quietly prove something else. We have no published evidence that it does. What is wanted A small corpus of known cases where a statement's meaning or hypotheses changed across a Lean/Mathlib version (a definition changed, a hypothesis became implicit, a default changed), each as a pair of Lean files for the old and new toolchain, and a report of whether Gate 2 accepts, refuses or cannot process the translation of each. Include cases it should accept, so we also see false refusals. Done when A directory with at least ten cases, a script that runs them, and a short write-up of what was caught and what was missed. Missed cases become issues. Related: 281 (the catalogue of toolchain changes). Difficulty: hard. Needs the translation pipeline running locally (emissary-archangel)…
descriptions.github:5707629843: Context Tengoku moves projects between Lean versions. A theorem can break, or silently change meaning, in a bump. What is wanted A catalogue (a document in docs/ , one section per category) of the kinds of change between toolchain releases, each with a real example found in Lean or Mathlib release notes, changelogs or commit history, and a note on whether it breaks compilation or changes meaning: renames and deprecations, removed lemmas, changed definitions or defeq behaviour, changed simp / ext attributes, instance priorities, universe handling, elaboration changes (coercions, unification, autoImplicit -style options), changed default options, notation changes, tactic behaviour. Done when At least ten categories, each with a cited example. Mark which categories the current entailment check would catch…
descriptions.github:5707629430: Context It is hard to tell from the documentation which of Tengoku's checks are running in CI now and which are planned or in progress (for example the nightly independent kernel check with nanoda, provenance and credit checks, the vacuity check, the axiom scan). What is wanted One table in docs/ with a row per check: what it checks, what it cannot catch, the workflow and script that run it (link them), when it runs (every PR, merge queue, promotion, nightly), and its status: running , in progress or planned . Reading workflow files; no code changes.
descriptions.github:5707629115: Context A translation is accepted only if the translated script compiles in the Tengoku environment and the kernel accepts fun h = h : T translated → T original (the entailment check, "Gate 2", implemented in emissary-archangel gate2/ ). What exactly is replayed from the original's lean4export dump: statements and the definitions that give them meaning only, or proofs too? How are statement-only theorems added? 3. A same-named declaration already in the environment (for example from Mathlib or core): when is the original's reference identified with it, and…

descriptions.github:5707023329: The README's own strongest caveat: nginx returning a fixed string is close to the worst case for a mesh, because the proxy's work is a large fraction of total work. descriptions.github:5704817391: Describe the bug With MariaDB's default REPEATABLE-READ , header storage hits lock waits and deadlocks under load (binaries + backfill + release processing at once). Why it matters Jobs declare the GPU APIs they can use ( gpu.apis any ), and Oarbank places them only where one really exists. For Linux containers under WSL, the agent currently reports: - directml for any GPU; - cuda for NVIDIA only. We don't know what AMD and Intel GPUs actually get in a container. If the agent claims an API that doesn't work, jobs fail on your machine. If it misses one that works, your GPU sits idle. Background: the Windows containers design note and the GPU placement how-to. descriptions.github:5704424344: Who can help A Windows 10 or 11 PC (x64 or arm64) with an NVIDIA GPU and a current NVIDIA Windows driver. Allow about an hour. Why it matters This is the path that lets a Windows gaming or workstation PC run GPU jobs in a container, the same way it would on a Linux box: image generation, LLM batch work, transcription. The agent runs Linux container jobs with Microsoft's WSL containers (WSLc), in a session and VM of its own; it never touches your WSL distributions. A job that asks for gpus = "all" gets the GPU through WSLc's CDI device ( cdi:microsoft.com/wslc ). CI runs this on a GitHub Windows runner, which has no GPU, so it has never run on a real NVIDIA card. Background: the Windows containers design note and the GPU placement how-to. descriptions.github:5704423042: Oarbank 2.5 runs batch jobs across the Macs, Linux machines and Windows PCs you own: - jobs find the GPU APIs each machine really has; - GPU jobs can run inside containers; - the coordinator itself runs on Windows. descriptions.github:5704359781: Why it matters wordlist-gen feeds subenum, so its mistakes surface later as confusing subenum errors. Evidence - Silent overwrite. The default -o wordlist.txt overwrites an existing file in the current directory with no prompt ( tools/wordlist-gen.go:119,133 ). - Empty output exits 0. -common=false with no -domain or -combine writes an empty file, exits 0 and prints "0 unique entries". subenum then fails with "no valid entries". - No validation of -combine prefixes. Prefixes such as shop! or a b are written out, and subenum later silently skips them. Suggested approach - Refuse to overwrite an existing file without -f . - Exit non-zero when 0 entries are produced. - Validate entries with the same label rules as internal/wordlist . descriptions.github:5704266826: Math ( kernel/src/java/lang/Math.java ) has no overflow-checked arithmetic yet. Add the int and long versions of addExact , subtractExact , multiplyExact , negateExact , incrementExact , plus toIntExact(long) . They throw ArithmeticException on overflow with the JDK's messages: "integer overflow" for int , "long overflow" for long . The JDK implementations use neat bit tricks to detect overflow without wider types. Worth reading. Done when: conformance tests cover normal results and overflow at the edges ( Integer.MAX VALUE + 1 , Long.MIN VALUE -1 , ...), comparing the exception messages. New here? descriptions.github:5704266733: Common String transforms are missing from kernel/src/java/lang/String.java . Add toUpperCase() , toLowerCase() , repeat(int) and replace(char, char) . descriptions.github:5703932297: Description findRegisteredComponents in lib/core/tooling/componentTagNaming.js caches its result per directory and never invalidates it: There is no clearCache , no mtime check and nothing watching the directory. In a short-lived eslint CLI run that is harmless — the process exits. In a long-lived one it is not: the VS Code ESLint extension runs a persistent server, and so does eslint --watch -style tooling. So a component created after the first lint of a project is absent from the registry for the rest of that process's life. Because findInvalidComponentTags only reports a tag when a registered component matches it case-insensitively, the consequence is a silent false negative: avenx/component-tag-naming simply stops catching the mistake it exists to catch. Reproduction In an editor this shows up as: add a component, write its tag in lower case, get no warning — then restart the…

descriptions.github:5703650114: The app speaks eight languages, the README only English and Bosnian ( README.bs.md ). Learners of Bosnian often live in Germany, Austria, Scandinavia, the Netherlands, France or Turkey. What to do - Translate README.md into one language you speak natively: German, Turkish, Swedish, Dutch, Norwegian Bokmål, Danish or French, as README. .md (e.g. README.tr.md ). - Keep code blocks, file names, badges and Bosnian words exactly as they are. - Add your language to the language line at the top of README.md and README.bs.md . - Please no machine translation without checking it yourself: say in the PR that you are a native speaker. One language per PR; comment here with the language you take so nobody does the same one twice. Done when python3 -m pytest passes (it checks links).
descriptions.github:5703649619: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explains data flow, content model and quality gates with Mermaid diagrams, but not what happens when a release is made. What to do Read .github/workflows/release.yml and .github/workflows/pypi.yml and add a section "Releases" with one Mermaid diagram (flowchart or sequence) showing: manual start with a tag → tests and daten exportieren.py --pruefen → dataset zip, Anki packages ( anki bauen.py ), checksums → GitHub release → PyPI workflow (and the optional Hugging Face upload). A few sentences of text are enough. tests/test mermaid.py checks the diagrams; keep it green. Done when python3 -m pytest passes and the diagram renders on GitHub.
descriptions.github:5703649154: People who find the dataset in data/ need a quick "how do I use this?" example. What to do 1. Add docs/examples/quiz.py : a terminal quiz (standard library only) that reads data/vocabulary.json , lets the user pick a level and a language ( --level 3 --lang en ), asks ten words in random order (Bosnian → meaning) and prints the score. Accept answers case-insensitively. 2. Add docs/examples/README.md explaining how to run it and pointing to data/DATASHEET.md for the fields and the licence (CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution required). 3. Add a test in tests/ that runs the quiz with fixed answers (e.g. pass a --seed and feed input), so the example cannot break silently when the data format changes. 4. Link the example from the dataset section of README.md . Done when python3 -m pytest and ruff check . pass and reuse lint is happy.
descriptions.github:5703648583: The package zmaj-bosnian (source in paket/src/zmaj bosnian/ ) gives Python access to the course: vocabulary() , levels() , sentences() , stories() … but there is no command line. What to do Add paket/src/zmaj bosnian/ main .py (standard library only, argparse ): - python -m zmaj bosnian word [--lang en] prints one random word: Bosnian and its meaning. - python -m zmaj bosnian search kuća [--lang en] finds words whose Bosnian or meaning contains the text. - python -m zmaj bosnian stats prints the counts from counts() . Use only the public functions in init .py . Add a test in tests/test paket.py that runs the three commands (see how the existing test puts paket/src on sys.path ) and mention the commands in paket/README.md . Done when python3 -m pytest and ruff check . pass. Python 3.10+, no new dependencies.
descriptions.github:5703648023: The open dataset in data/ has JSON Schemas for vocabulary , sentences , stories and parallel (in data/schema/ ), but not for glossary.json , grammar.json and manifest.json . What to do 1. Look at the existing schemas, e.g. data/schema/vocabulary.schema.json (Draft 2020-12), and at the three JSON files. 2. Write data/schema/glossary.schema.json , grammar.schema.json and manifest.schema.json by hand in the same style (the schemas are not generated; daten exportieren.py only writes the data). 3. Add the names to the parametrized test json schema in tests/test datensatz.py . 4. If data/DATASHEET.md lists the schemas, add the new ones there too. Done when python3 -m pytest , ruff check . and python3 daten exportieren.py --pruefen pass. No Bosnian knowledge needed.

When one of these codes appears, the integration logs a one-time warning that starts with Canada Post return event seen . What would help: paste that log line in a comment, together with the matching line from the Canada Post tracking page. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5703531485: When a parcel is waiting for you at a post office or parcel locker, it should show as at pickup point , with the office's name and town as the pickup point. The office name is confirmed on real parcels, but so far only after the parcel had already moved on, never while the parcel was still waiting. When a parcel is waiting for collection, the integration logs a one-time warning that starts with Canada Post parcel waiting at a pickup point . What would help: paste that log line in a comment and say whether the parcel sensor showed at pickup point with the right office. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5703531345: Canada Post usually gives only an expected delivery date , so the integration shows the date as an all-day event and has never seen an actual delivery time window. Canada Post's app knows a window with a start and end time, so some parcels probably carry one. When a parcel with a window comes in, the integration logs a one-time warning that starts with Canada Post delivery window seen and shows the window's shape. What would help: paste that log line in a comment, together with the time window the Canada Post tracking page showed for the same parcel. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.

descriptions.github:5701690995: Description: The pipeline starts with decoding IMD's raw daily .grd rainfall files into a usable format. This script is the entry point for all later work (masking, ConvLSTM, indices), so it's a good place to begin. Background: IMD publishes 0.25° gridded daily rainfall as single-precision float binary (.grd). Each file is one day and decodes to a 129 × 135 array. The extent is Lat 6.5°N–38.5°N, Lon 66.5°E–100.0°E. Missing values are flagged as 99.9 or -99.9. Tasks: Create scripts/decode imd binary.py. Write decode grd(path) - xarray.DataArray using np.fromfile(..., dtype=np.float32) reshaped to (129, 135). Attach lat (6.5→38.5) and lon (66.5→100.0) coordinates at 0.25° spacing. Mask 99.9 and -99.9 to NaN. Add a function to stack multiple daily files along a time axis and save to CF-compliant NetCDF4 (data/processed/IMD Gridded Rainfall 0.25 Real v4.nc, variable rainfall, with units and…
descriptions.github:5701675565: What: 14 trains are excluded because two stations print the same time and their order can't be determined. Examples: Lucknow and Lucknow Jn, Udaipur and Udaipur City, Ernakulam Town and Ernakulam Jn. These are genuinely different stations. The full list is in scripts/tag/excluded trains.csv . Ideas: the row order inside a single TAG table, distances (the km columns), or the train's direction of travel can often fix the order. Rules: recover a train only when the order is certain. Spot-check recovered trains against eRail (running days, stops on route, day numbers) and include validate.py --sample 150 output before and after. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
descriptions.github:5701675249: What: these names still have no code in the official timetable: Kalol (KLL/KLLF, 15 stops), Dhaulpur (DHO/DHOA, 11), Jetalsar (8) and Phalodi (PLC/PLCJ, 6, which are probably the same station under two codes). Why they're unresolved: the route-context rule requires every candidate code to appear in the 2016 routes before it can rule one out. For these names, one candidate is missing from those routes, so a "no routes" result proves nothing. Ideas: - Check whether the pair is really one station under two codes. If so, propose a group for data/station equivalences.json with two independent pieces of evidence (see scripts/tag/build equivalences.py ). - Otherwise, find other evidence such as the line, the table or gauge notes. Rules: never guess. Include validate.py --sample 150 output before and after, and the eRail spot-check results. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
descriptions.github:5701675046: What: 47 stops named "Sabarmati" in Trains at a Glance 2026 have no station code. Two codes fit (SBI, Sabarmati Jn BG, and SBT, Sabarmati), and the current route-context rule can't pick one because both appear on the same 2016 routes. Where: scripts/tag/stations.py and the ambiguity rule in scripts/tag/build.py ; the candidates are listed in scripts/tag/station ambiguous.csv . Ideas: the line or table the stop sits on (TAG tables follow one line), the train's direction (towards Ahmedabad Jn vs the Botad/meter-gauge side), or the platform/side notes in the PDF. Rules: never guess. Resolve a stop only when the evidence clearly picks one code; otherwise leave it null. Check resolved stops against eRail routes and include python3 scripts/tag/validate.py --sample 150 output before and after in the PR. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

descriptions.github:5701649401: 概要 / Summary --palette auto ( mvcodec/auto palette.py ) は RGB 空間で K-Means を行い、各クラスタ中心に RGB 距離が最も近いブロックを選んでいます。一方、GPU の減色処理は OkLab (知覚的に均等な色空間) で色を合わせています。パレット選択も OkLab で行えば、人の目で見た色の再現性が上がるはずです。 The automatic palette runs K-Means and nearest-block matching in RGB, while GPU quantization matches colors in OkLab. Doing the palette selection in OkLab should improve perceived color accuracy. ヒント / Hints - RGB → OkLab 変換は mvcodec/color.py の rgb to oklab torch() があります。 - 距離計算は DirectML でも動くよう mvcodec/device.py の squared distances() を使ってください ( torch.cdist は DirectML で使えない場合があります)。 - 効果の確認には benchmark/run.py の ΔE2000 が使えます。変更前後の数値を PR に載せてもらえると助かります。
descriptions.github:5701649212: 今は指定した幅・高さの中に、縦横比を保ったまま中央寄せ (余白は黒) で収めています。16:9 の動画を 128×128 にすると上下に黒い帯ができ、ブロックが無駄になります。動画を追加したときに縦横比を読み取り、黒帯が出ない幅・高さ (例: 128×72) を提案するボタンかプリセットがあると便利です。 Videos are letterboxed into the chosen width × height. A 16:9 video at 128×128 wastes blocks on black bars. Add a button or preset that reads the video's aspect ratio and suggests a matching size (e.g. 128×72). ヒント / Hints - 縦横比は ffprobe -v error -select streams v:0 -show entries stream=width,height -of csv=p=0 < 動画 で取得できます (ffmpeg のパスは video player gui.get ffmpeg path() と同じ場所にあります)。 - 幅・高さの入力欄は video player gui.py の self.width var / self.height var です。 - 最大 512 ブロックを超えないようにしてください。
descriptions.github:5701648997: benchmark/metrics/ms ssim.py の calculate ms ssim() は未実装で、常に nan を返しています。マルチスケール SSIM を実装して、ベンチマーク結果に実際の値が出るようにしたいです。 calculate ms ssim() in benchmark/metrics/ms ssim.py is a stub that always returns nan . Implement multi-scale SSIM so the benchmark reports a real value. ヒント / Hints - 同じフォルダの ssim.py は scikit-image の structural similarity を使っています。各スケールで SSIM (またはコントラスト・構造成分) を計算し、2 倍ずつ縮小して重み付き積を取るのが標準的な方法です (Wang et al., 2003)。 - 入力は (H, W, 3) の uint8 画像 2 枚です。64×64 など小さい画像ではスケール数を減らす必要があります。 - 動作確認: pip install -r requirements-benchmark.txt の後 python benchmark/run.py --video < 動画 --output out.js --fps 10 - 小さな単体テストを tests/ に追加してもらえると助かります。

descriptions.github:5701408453: get trend ( mcp server/tools.py ) loads values with ORDER BY effective at ASC LIMIT 500 . When a marker has more than 500 values in the window (daily wearable data: steps, calories, resting HR over 5 years), the oldest 500 are kept and the most recent ones are dropped — so the trend ignores exactly the latest months. Task - Keep the most recent 500 values (e.g. ORDER BY effective at DESC LIMIT 500 in a subquery, then sort ascending for Mann-Kendall), or aggregate daily/weekly before the trend. - Return the date range actually used ( from / to ) next to n , so the model can say what the trend covers. - Add a test in tests/test mcp tools.py with 500 synthetic points where only the recent tail changes direction.

descriptions.github:5700955023: Logbeam recognises the usual level words ( ERROR , WARN , FATAL , SEVERE , NOTICE , DBG , …). Some systems use their own, e.g. ALERT , EMERG , CRIT , AUDIT , or a localized word. Idea: a "Levels" section on the Settings page where you map your own words to ERROR / WARN / INFO / DEBUG / TRACE. Where: - level detection: detectLevel and LEVEL ALIASES in src/lib/logs.ts ; - settings: src/shared/settings.ts and src/options/ ; - big logs are parsed in a Web Worker ( src/content/parseWorker.ts ), so the custom words have to be passed to the worker with the text, or applied after parsing like custom secret patterns are (see openViewer in src/content/logViewer.ts ). Done when a word added in Settings is detected in the viewer, with a unit test and an e2e check.
descriptions.github:5700954476: The viewer, Compare and Settings pages are always dark. Some people read logs on a light screen or print them. Idea: follow the browser's prefers-color-scheme , with an override in Settings (Auto / Dark / Light). Where: the colours are CSS variables at the top of src/content/viewerStyles.ts , src/diff/diff.css , src/options/options.css and src/viewer/viewer.css . A light set of the same variables under (prefers-color-scheme: light) is most of the work. Level colours ( --error , --warn , …), highlights ( .hl-0 … .hl-4 ) and pod colours ( .src-0 … .src-7 ) need light-friendly versions with enough contrast. Done when both themes are readable, and the screenshots from npm run e2e look right in both.
descriptions.github:5700952563: Logbeam's UI can be translated through locales/ /messages.json ; English ( en ) and Ukrainian ( uk ) are there now. The browser picks the language automatically. To add a language: 1. Copy locales/en/messages.json to locales/ /messages.json (codes: de , pl , es , pt BR , …). 2. Translate each message . Keep {page} placeholders as they are, and keep the tool names like camelCase and CONSTANT untranslated. 3. Keep the text on popup buttons short: the tool buttons have room for about 13 characters. 4. Run npm run build , load dist/ in Chrome with that browser language and check the popup. One language per pull request is perfect. Native speakers especially welcome!

descriptions.github:5699598310: Summary tm.load multichannel csv reads rows with csv.DictReader , which drops blank lines without a word. In a regularly sampled record a blank line is a missing sample on every channel, so skipping it shortens the record and shifts every later sample in time. tm.load sensors already rejects this case (see the 2.0.0 changelog and the comment in src/timoshenko/sensors.py ); the multi-channel loader should behave the same way. Reproduction Expected A ValueError naming the line, as load sensors raises for a one-column file. Where - src/timoshenko/multichannel.py , load multichannel csv : read with csv.reader as load sensors does, or otherwise detect skipped lines through reader.line num . - tests/ : a test that fails before the change and passes after it. - docs/changelog.md : one line under "Unreleased".

descriptions.github:5699538128: RFC 9728 lets protected resource metadata list bearer methods supported ( header , body , query ). See CONTRIBUTING.md for setup and the test command. Comment here to claim it; small PRs are welcome.

descriptions.github:5699532606: packages/jwt-tools/src/jwt.ts verifies HS and RS tokens. ECDSA tokens are common (Apple, many OIDC providers) and need only node:crypto : crypto.verify("sha256", input, { key, dsaEncoding: "ieee-p1363" }, signature) because JWS encodes ECDSA signatures as raw r || s , not DER. The curve must match the algorithm (P-256 for ES256, P-384 for ES384, P-521 for ES512). Where to look: packages/jwt-tools/src/jwt.ts, packages/jwt-tools/src/index.ts, packages/jwt-tools/test/server.test.mjs, packages/jwt-tools/README.md, CHANGELOG.md. descriptions.github:5696899886: Found while reviewing PR 430 (issue 425), which made ack() refuse an envelope with no delivery tag and mirrored reject() . The mirroring exposed that the two halves never actually behaved alike, in two ways. 1. reject() has a side effect before it throws; ack() does not So a refused reject() has already flushed and reset that queue's pendingAcks and unacked , while the refused ack() added in 425 leaves both untouched. Both throw, but the state afterwards differs. This is why PR 430 had to soften its claim that "the two halves of the same envelope contract now behave alike" — the messages are genuinely identical in shape (same Cannot the message received from queue "%s" template, same exception class, same queue name), the behaviour is not. 2. An unknown queue name throws in reject() and is silently ignored in ack() Same envelope, same invalid state, opposite outcomes: reject() tells…

descriptions.github:5696769990: scripts/install/patch-scripts-tree.sh rewrites a maintainer script's shebang to !$INSTDIR/usr/bin/dn-shell (the launcher, which turns on the path shim). It misses some, which keep !$INSTDIR/usr/bin/dash and then run without the shim — their /etc , /usr reads hit Android's real root. On the reference prefix the missed ones are ca-certificates , cpp , figlet , gcc , libcrypt-dev (5 of 22 postinst s). Symptom and a minimal repro are in docs/reference/known-issues.md , "Maintainer scripts with a raw interpreter shebang" — e.g. dpkg --configure ca-certificates fails with sed: can't read /etc/ca-certificates.conf . Fix: rewrite every maintainer-script shebang, not a subset, and verify ca-certificates configures and figlet resolves.

descriptions.github:5696677851: Problem tests/conftest.py does import llmsql.inference.inference vllm at module level, which imports vllm . Contributors without a GPU / without the multi-GB vllm extra can't run any test (collection fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm' ). Proposal - Move vLLM-specific fixtures into tests/inference/conftest.py guarded with pytest.importorskip("vllm") , or mock the module in sys.modules . - Add pytest markers ( gpu , slow , integration ) and run a fast CPU-only job on every PR, plus the full matrix (3.10–3.12) on main. - Document pytest -m "not gpu" in CONTRIBUTING.md.
descriptions.github:5696677507: Problem llmsql/ cli/evaluate.py:: execute wraps evaluate() in try/except Exception and just print s the error. The process then exits with code 0, so scripts / CI pipelines think evaluation succeeded. Proposal Log the error and sys.exit(1) (or simply let it propagate), and add a CLI test asserting a non-zero exit code on a missing outputs file. Also replace the hard-coded choices=["1.0", "2.0"] in both CLI commands with get available versions() from llmsql.config .
descriptions.github:5696677370: Problem Several CLI flags are declared as action="store true" with default=True , so they are always True and there is no way to turn them off from the command line: - llmsql/ cli/inference.py — --trust-remote-code (transformers & vLLM), --use-chat-template (vLLM), --do-sample for vLLM (default True ) - llmsql/ cli/evaluate.py — --show-mismatches Consequences: e.g. greedy decoding can't be requested for the vLLM CLI via --do-sample (only by passing --temperature 0 ), and remote code is always trusted. Proposal Use argparse.BooleanOptionalAction (Python ≥3.9) so both --flag and --no-flag exist, and add CLI tests for both forms. Related: trust remote code=True by default is a security footgun (executes arbitrary code from the Hub). Consider defaulting to False in a minor release with a deprecation note. Also: vLLM --do-sample uses add common generation args(..., 1.0, True) , and default…

descriptions.github:5696211833: Problem pi to pi() in src/components/common/angle lib.py wraps an angle only once, so angles beyond ±3π are not normalized. descriptions.github:5695832624: Problem With rootless podman as the container runtime, the PowerShell installer tests pull the PowerShell image once per test home. One local ./mvnw verify with SYMPHONY TRELLO TEST PWSH=./scripts/pwsh-docker.sh created about 16 GB of image storage under the test temp directory. With the default java.io.tmpdir , the same data goes to /tmp , which is a RAM-backed tmpfs on many Linux hosts. There it fills the filesystem and eats memory, and other runs fail with EDQUOT . descriptions.github:5695769902: Description Root package.json declares engines.node = 20 and packageManager: , but there is no .npmrc , so the engines field is advisory — pnpm won't fail on an unsupported Node version. Add a root .npmrc with engine-strict=true so a wrong Node version is caught at install time. Scope - Add a root .npmrc containing engine-strict=true (and optionally auto-install-peers=true to match the current pnpm defaults, if confirmed consistent with the lockfile). - Verify pnpm install --frozen-lockfile still succeeds on Node 20/22. Out of scope - Changing engines or packageManager . Acceptance criteria - [ ] .npmrc enforces the engines constraint without breaking install on supported Node versions. - [ ] pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build && pnpm test pass. Where to start - .npmrc (new) - package.json ( engines , packageManager ) Estimated effort Small ( 15 min).

descriptions.github:5695009242: Our packages are ESM, and Node only loads ESM when relative imports carry their file extension ( ./runtime.js , not ./runtime ). The TypeScript sources use extensionless imports, so every package's build runs scripts/fix-esm-imports.ts after tsc to add the extensions to the emitted dist/ . Today every published package loads fine with plain Node. Nothing checks that it stays that way, though: if a new package forgets the fix-esm-imports step, or a new import pattern slips past the script, the published package breaks for users with ERR MODULE NOT FOUND . Our tests would not notice, because Vitest and tsx resolve extensionless paths on their own. What to do 1. Add scripts/check-esm-imports.ts that, after a build: - finds every non-private package under packages/ - imports each one with plain Node, for example by running node --input-type=module -e "await import(' ')" with the package…

descriptions.github:5694948019: Context The section Re-derivation and early cutoff in docs/architecture.md (around line 88) says propagate() walks the beliefs to re-derive "in creation order". That was true early on, but it caused wrong results when beliefs were created in the same instant (coarse clocks on Windows). Today the kernel orders them by dependency : a belief is re-derived only after the beliefs among its inputs that also need re-deriving. Creation time, then the key, only break ties. See rederive candidates in src/corollary/kernel.py . What to do 1. Rewrite that sentence in docs/architecture.md to describe the dependency order and the tie-break, and say why it matters: a conclusion is never re-derived from an input that is itself about to change. 2. Search the rest of docs/ for other descriptions of the order (for example in docs/concepts.md and docs/guides/belief-base.md ) and make them consistent…

descriptions.github:5694684484: Problem Common actions (start conversion, preview plan, remove selected file, switch tabs) require pointer interaction only. Why users care Keyboard shortcuts speed up repeated desktop workflows and improve accessibility. Tasks - [ ] Add shortcuts, e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to start, Ctrl/Cmd+P for preview, Delete/Backspace to remove selection - [ ] Show shortcut hints in tooltips/menus - [ ] Avoid conflicts with OS/Electron defaults - [ ] Ensure shortcuts are disabled while modal dialogs are open / when busy (except cancel if available) - [ ] Document shortcuts in About or a Help panel Acceptance criteria - Documented shortcuts work on Linux, Windows, and macOS modifiers - No shortcut triggers conversion accidentally while typing in inputs Size S
descriptions.github:5694683955: Problem Long conversions give no OS-level signal when finished if the user has switched to another app. Why users care Notifications restore attention for OCR/PDF batches without keeping the window focused. Tasks - [ ] Show a system notification on completion (success, partial failure, cancelled) - [ ] Include short summary counts - [ ] Respect OS permission / quiet modes; fail soft if unsupported - [ ] Avoid notifying for very short jobs if that is noisy (optional threshold) - [ ] Clicking notification focuses the app when possible Acceptance criteria - Backgrounded app notifies when a job set finishes - Notification text matches the in-app summary - No crash if notifications are denied Size S
descriptions.github:5694683862: Problem Results provide “Open folder” via shell.openPath on the directory, but not reveal/open for a specific successful output file. Why users care After converting one or a few files, opening the exact result is the fastest verification path. Tasks - [ ] Add “Open file” and/or “Reveal in folder” actions per successful result row - [ ] Use the correct OS APIs ( shell.openPath / shell.showItemInFolder ) - [ ] Disable/hide actions for failed jobs - [ ] Handle missing files after external deletion gracefully Acceptance criteria - Users can open a specific output from the results list - Folder reveal selects the file where the OS supports it Size S
descriptions.github:5694683119: Problem Animated GIF/WebP inputs can be converted via Sharp, but animation is effectively lost (typically first frame) without a clear warning. Users may think the full animation was preserved. Why users care Silent data loss destroys trust. An explicit policy and warning prevent surprises. Tasks - [ ] Detect multi-frame / animated inputs when inexpensive - [ ] Warn during convert/dry-run that only the first frame will be used (or document and enforce a chosen policy) - [ ] Optionally add --first-frame / future --coalesce placeholders - [ ] Mention the limitation in README/formats help - [ ] Test that animated fixtures produce a warning Acceptance criteria - Animated inputs never fail silently without user-visible notice - Still convert usefully by default (first frame) unless a better policy is chosen Size S
descriptions.github:5694682750: Problem Commander flags, presets, and subcommands are hard to discover. There is no completion script for common shells. descriptions.github:5694668154: The web app now has a mixer, the pen's own sound and an in-browser drawing reader. The iPad app in ios/ has none of them yet, and its Gemini prompt still follows the old rules. It's a big one, so pick a piece: - the pen's sound ( src/audio/touch.ts ) - the new prompt rules ( src/llm/planner.ts → ios/Skuzic/LLM/Planner.swift ) - the mixer ( src/ui/Mixer.tsx ) - reading the drawing on device (SigLIP 2 through Core ML) Comment with the piece you're taking so two people don't build the same thing.
descriptions.github:5694668054: The drawing reader looks at the whole page as one picture. But a drawing has more in it than what it shows: where the marks land, how fast you draw, how hard you press. Some ideas to try: - fast, scratchy strokes push Energy up; slow ones calm it down - the pen's notes sit where you draw: left on the page, left in your headphones - pressing hard brings the lead sound forward src/vision/ink.ts already turns the page into two numbers (how much ink, how warm the colours are) that nudge Energy and Brightness. That's the pattern to follow. Stroke speed and pressure are available in src/ui/DrawCanvas.tsx , and src/audio/touch.ts already measures speed for the pen's sound. Try one idea and tell us in the PR whether it made drawing feel more musical. "It didn't" is a useful answer too.
descriptions.github:5694667620: Magenta RT can be told which notes to play, frame by frame, through a 128-key piano roll. Today the bridge only uses that to hold the band to a chord loop in F major. It could follow your pen instead: a line that climbs could become a rising melody, a zigzag a trill. Where to start - server/magenta bridge.py : the Harmony class builds the notes input for every chunk. - src/ui/DrawCanvas.tsx already knows every stroke's points and timing. Open questions - Which octave, and should it stay in F major? (Probably, since the pen plays in F.) - How long should a drawn phrase keep playing after you lift the pen? - Should every stroke make a melody, or only one colour, or only when you ask? You need a Mac with Apple Silicon to run the bridge. server/README.md has the setup.
descriptions.github:5694667527: The pen's piano always plays in F major. If you change the key in the mixer (Feel → Tempo, key and more), the band moves to the new key but the pen doesn't, and they clash. The pen's notes are MIDI numbers in src/audio/touch.ts ( NOTES , and HOME for where phrases come to rest). Shifting them by the distance between F and the chosen key should be most of it. The key lives in state.config.scale (Lyria's Scale enum), so DrawCanvas needs to pass it along to the pen. Done when: pick D / Bm, draw for a bit, and the pen sounds at home with the band.
descriptions.github:5694667429: When you lift the pen, skuzic picks a mood and two instruments from a small, hand-written palette in src/vision/palette.json : 9 moods and 10 instruments. It's the easiest way to change how skuzic sounds, and you don't need to know anything about audio. Some ideas: snow, outer space, a city at night, a kalimba that only shows up for flowers. Or whatever you'd want to hear when you draw your favourite thing. How 1. Add an entry to palette.json . A mood needs a short prompt ("hushed and starlit") and a few tags describing drawings it should match ("a crescent moon", "a starry night sky"). An instrument needs a prompt ("gentle harp arpeggios") and its own tags. 2. Run scripts/embed-palette.py (the command is at the top of the file). pnpm test fails until you do, on purpose. 3. Draw something that should trigger it. The mixer's History tab tells you what it heard ("Feels like rain: felt…
descriptions.github:5694581191: Context Agent.run() returns a Report whose steps hold the exact prompt, the raw response and each action's verdict. Nothing records what a step cost . Proposal (open to discussion) - Let an adapter report usage without breaking custom models. One option is an optional last usage attribute that the agent reads after each call. Another is letting complete() return a str subclass that carries the usage. Please propose a design in a comment before…

descriptions.github:5694580973: Context When a belief cites a document, Corollary checks that the quote actually states the value, at the scale its unit says. For example, 4.3e9 matches "$4.3 billion" and "$4.3B", but not "$4 million". The provenance check uses the same matching. The units are English only. A Brazilian or Spanish filing that says "receita de 4.3 bilhões" doesn't match 4.3e9 , so kb.cite() raises CitationError on a correct citation. What to do In src/corollary/textmatch.py , add these words to UNIT and UNIT SCALES , in singular and plural, with and without accents: | Word | Scale | |---|---| | mil | thousand ( 1e-3 ) | | milhão / milhões , millón / millones | million ( 1e-6 ) | | bilhão / bilhões | billion ( 1e-9 ) | | trilhão / trilhões , billón / billones | trillion ( 1e-12 ) | Note that Spanish billón means 10^12, not 10^9. Spanish "mil millones" (10^9) and decimal commas ("4,3") are out of scope…

Share the logic through /server-shared so all adapters behave the same, and update the OpenAPI description there. This touches several packages, so please comment here…

descriptions.github:5694316881: Quail refuses ORDER BY, OFFSET, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, and plain column predicates in WHERE. Users apply them on the client or in the source database. Semantic top-k, the most wanted query, cannot be written: Plan Three PRs, grouped by the machinery they share. Everything runs on the coordinator in Arrow; the GPU executor changes only where noted. Only the Quail planners (standard and reranker) get new nodes. The stock vLLM and SGLang planners refuse the new clauses, so a query with one runs on Quail only. PR 1: ordering and the limit rule. 187. ORDER BY, OFFSET, top-k, and DISTINCT, since all four are fields on the root Project and one coordinator node. - Sort keys, offset, and a distinct flag become fields on the root Project, beside LIMIT. - One Sort node: select-k when there is a LIMIT, full sort otherwise. DISTINCT is an Acero aggregate with no functions in the same node. - Limit…

descriptions.github:5694218948: Description avenx stats prints every compiler diagnostic twice. No other command that compiles does. With one undeclared template reference in a project: bin/commands/stats.js compiles the project twice. It calls buildModel(cli) at line 92, which compiles and reports diagnostics, and then re-runs the parser per file to measure compiled template size: extractTemplate re-runs template validation, so every warning is reported a second time. The comment above that block says it collects things "the way compileUnit collects it, so the validation sees" the same inputs — the duplication is a side effect of that deliberate second pass, and it went unnoticed. Besides the doubled output, it means avenx stats does roughly twice the compile work it needs to. Reproduction Goal avenx stats should report each diagnostic once. Suggested implementation Two routes, and it is worth looking at both before…
descriptions.github:5694215877: Found in a post-merge review of 93 (issue 76). rootCmd sets neither SilenceUsage nor SilenceErrors , so cobra prints: The message itself is clear, which is what the CHANGELOG claims, so this is cosmetic — but this is the second time a bad CLI argument produces a confusing screen (the first was the same port flag, before 93 validated it). Definition of done: - SilenceUsage: true on webCmd (or the root), so a runtime flag error is not followed by the full help - decide explicitly whether SilenceErrors stays off (the error is then printed once, by cobra, and os.Exit still gets a non-zero code) and note the choice in the code - a test asserting an invalid port does not print "Usage:" — or a short manual note in AGENTS.md if this is not testable in the current CLI test setup - bin/lint.sh green
descriptions.github:5694215001: Description A reference to an AVX PUBLIC variable that has no value is replaced with the literal undefined and nothing says so. replaceEnvVariables in lib/env.js : So a typo — process.env.AVX PUBLIC API URLL — compiles to undefined , the build reports success, and the application receives undefined wherever it expected a URL. The failure surfaces later as a fetch to undefined/users or a blank value in the UI, with nothing connecting it back to the misspelled variable. A forgotten .env entry in CI produces the same thing, which is the case where it costs the most: the build that was supposed to catch it is the build that silently shipped it. The compiler has a diagnostic for exactly this shape of problem elsewhere — AVX W03 for an undeclared template reference, AVX W40 for state nothing reads — but nothing for an environment variable that was referenced and never set. descriptions.github:5694214853: Found in a post-merge review of 93 (issue 76). validatePort rejects 0 ( n < 1 ). Before that change, tokeneks web --port 0 bound an ephemeral port and started serving normally — the printed URL was wrong ( but the command worked. Rejecting 0 is the right call for a CLI that prints a URL built from the flag, so this is not a defect — it is an unlisted behaviour change on a public flag. CHANGELOG.md says only that out-of-range ports now error. Definition of done: - CHANGELOG notes that port 0 is rejected, and why (the dashboard prints the URL it was given, so an ephemeral port is useless to the user) - one clause, same style as the existing entry

descriptions.github:5694213737: Found in a post-merge review of 93 (issue 76). validatePort has exactly one caller, and the test exercises only the helper. Two mutations both leave the suite green: 1. delete the if err := validatePort(port) block from runWeb → TestValidatePort still passes 2. move that block below openTokeneksStore() ( web.go:227 ) → still passes, and now a bad flag leaks a store handle and starts the watcher before failing What 76 asked for is fail-fast before the store opens , and nothing pins that. Where to start: web test.go . descriptions.github:5694130790: The English reads "brought forward no sacrifice for sins", which inverts Hebrews 10:12. The printed Greek has οὐδεμίαν, which is probably a corruption of οὗτος δὲ μίαν ("but this one [offered] one sacrifice"). Details: docs/FIDELITY ISSUES 20261003.md. Book: books/cyril-alexandria-adoration-1 How to fix: check another witness (another edition or manuscript reading) for this line, and translate it with the emendation marked if the witness supports it. Cite the witness in the pull request.
descriptions.github:5694130618: The English of the Origen Romans catena paraphrases the Greek and adds words it does not have, for example "through faith alone" (no μόνη in the Greek), εὐσέβειαν rendered "security" (it is "piety"), and "as if He arbitrarily chose some and rejected others" (not in the Greek). Details: docs/FIDELITY ISSUES 20261003.md. Book: books/origen-romans-catena How to fix: retranslate from the locked Greek following docs/START HERE.md. Do not copy any existing English translation.

descriptions.github:5693457949: Description In ExecutionProperties.java , bufferTimeout is annotated with: In Apache Flink ( ExecutionOptions.BUFFER TIMEOUT ), setting buffer-timeout to -1 (or -1ms ) is a standard and officially documented tuning mechanism: - buffer-timeout: 0 = Low latency mode; buffers are flushed immediately after each record, reducing throughput. - buffer-timeout: 100ms = Periodic flushing every 100ms. - buffer-timeout: -1 = Maximum throughput mode; periodic flushing is disabled, and network buffers are only transmitted when full. Because (millis = 0) rejects any duration with negative milliseconds, Flinkboot prevents operators from configuring buffer-timeout: -1 , making it impossible to enable maximum-throughput streaming execution via typed properties. descriptions.github:5693456809: Description In RestoreMode.java , RestoreMode.LEGACY is currently included as an option: In Apache Flink (since Flink 1.15), RestoreMode.LEGACY has been deprecated due to state ownership ambiguities: - Under LEGACY mode, Flink did not maintain clear file ownership between the original savepoint and newly taken checkpoints, risking silent state corruption if operators moved or deleted the original savepoint while the restored job was running. - Apache Flink strongly advises using NO CLAIM (default, safe: Flink leaves the original savepoint untouched and creates independent checkpoint files) or CLAIM (Flink assumes ownership of savepoint files). - Furthermore, RestoreMode.LEGACY is completely removed in Flink 2.0. Eliminating LEGACY now in milestone before the 1.0.0 release ensures users do not rely on an unsafe and obsolete mode. Expected Behavior 1. In RestoreMode.java , remove the…
descriptions.github:5693450673: Every parcel tracked so far came back with a single status, so the opt-in status history only ever holds the latest step. It is not known whether ICS Courier ever returns earlier steps for a parcel that is still on its way. What would help: if you track a parcel that is still in transit, turn on the status history and say in a comment whether it ever shows more than one entry, and how that compares with the steps on the ICS Courier tracking page. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5693450510: ICS Courier reports the time of a status without a time zone. The integration assumes it is Canadian local time and shows it as received, so the delivered time may be off by a few hours depending on where you and the parcel are. What would help: compare the delivered time on the parcel sensor with the time on the ICS Courier tracking page, and say in a comment which province the parcel was delivered in and whether the two match. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5693450302: So far only delivered parcels have been tracked, so the only status confirmed on a real parcel is delivered . Everything before that — picked up, in transit, out for delivery, a missed delivery, a parcel held at a depot — has not been seen yet and shows as unknown . The integration logs a one-shot WARNING starting with Unrecognised ICS Courier status whenever it meets a status it doesn't know. That line holds only ICS Courier's short status code. What would help: when you see that warning, paste the line into a comment here, together with what the ICS Courier tracking page said about the parcel at that moment. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.

descriptions.github:5693371408: Description In Apache Flink (since 1.13), the runtime state backend and checkpoint storage are decoupled into two distinct concerns: 1. State Backend : Manages in-flight working state during execution ( HashMapStateBackend , EmbeddedRocksDBStateBackend ). Configured via env.setStateBackend(...) . 2. Checkpoint Storage : Manages where and how durable snapshots are persisted ( JobManagerCheckpointStorage , FileSystemCheckpointStorage ). Configured via env.getCheckpointConfig().setCheckpointStorage(...) . Currently in Flinkboot: - checkpoint-storage is declared inside StateBackendProperties.java ( state-backend.checkpoint-storage ). - storage-uri is declared inside CheckpointingProperties.java ( checkpointing.storage-uri ). If only initial-backoff is specified (e.g. initial-backoff: 5m ), Flink applies its default max-backoff of 2m . At runtime, Flink throws IllegalArgumentException: initialBackoff cannot be greater than maxBackoff during environment initialization. 2. If only max-backoff is specified (e.g. max-backoff: 500ms ), Flink applies its default initial-backoff of 1s . At runtime, Flink throws IllegalArgumentException: initialBackoff cannot be greater than maxBackoff . Hardcoding Flink defaults into Flinkboot is fragile against upstream drift across Flink versions. Therefore, the robust fail-fast invariant is: If either initial-backoff or max-backoff is…

descriptions.github:5693246631: Description In Apache Flink's checkpointing architecture, min-pause-between-checkpoints specifies a mandatory rest duration between the completion of checkpoint $N$ and the triggering of checkpoint $N+1$. Concurrently, max-concurrent-checkpoints specifies how many checkpoints can be in-flight simultaneously. These two settings are mutually incompatible when min-pause-between-checkpoints 0 and max-concurrent-checkpoints 1 : Flink cannot trigger concurrent checkpoints while simultaneously enforcing a mandatory pause between them. Apache Flink enforces this invariant and throws an IllegalArgumentException at startup: Currently, CheckpointingPropertiesValidator does not validate this interdependency. If an operator sets both min-pause-between-checkpoints: 5s and max-concurrent-checkpoints: 2 , Flinkboot validation passes, only for Flink to fail at job startup. Expected Behavior In…

In multi-parallelism deployments, this causes: 1. JMX MBean name collisions ( InstanceAlreadyExistsException in Kafka metrics reporting). 2. descriptions.github:5692966647: A client sending a valid handshake with Upgrade: WebSocket (RFC 6455 section 4.2.1 says the value is case-insensitive) makes CanWorkWith return false, because the value is compared with == "websocket" . The handshake is never tried and the request falls through to normal HTTP handling, usually a 404. The Connection check on the same line is already case-insensitive. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/WebSocket/WebSocketService.cs:35-40 Fix: Compare with string.Equals(..., "websocket", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) .
descriptions.github:5692965880: WebServiceGroup.Clear() empties Services but does not unsubscribe Service PriorityChanged from the former members, unlike Remove and WebServiceCollection.Clear() . A cleared service that later changes its own Priority fires the handler, which re-inserts it into the cleared group, so it runs again on later requests. The group also stays referenced by every cleared service. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/WebServiceGroup.cs:67-70 Fix: Unsubscribe PriorityChanged from every service in Clear() before clearing, as WebServiceCollection.Clear() does.
descriptions.github:5692965646: SetSessionCookie casts MaxAge.TotalSeconds to int unchecked. A MaxAge above about 68 years (for example TimeSpan.FromDays(365 100) ) emits Max-Age=- on net8.0, so the browser deletes the session cookie immediately, while Expires stays correct. A much larger MaxAge makes DateTime.UtcNow + MaxAge throw. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/Sessions/SessionServiceBase.cs:132 Fix: Clamp the value to int.MaxValue before the cast and clamp the Expires computation to DateTime.MaxValue (or validate MaxAge in its setter).
descriptions.github:5692964597: An app sets MultipartFormData.StorageMapper for encryption at rest and receives an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body over UrlEncodedData.MaximumCacheSize (50 MB). The whole raw body is copied in plaintext to a temp FileStream that never passes through StorageMapper , while multipart parts, RawPostData and the per-value spill do use it. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/Post/UrlEncodedData.cs:104-113 Fix: Wrap rawFile with MultipartFormData.StorageMapper?.Invoke(task, file) ?? file like the other temp-file writes.
descriptions.github:5692963969: MultipartFormData matches parameter and token names case-sensitively, but RFC 9110/2045 make them case-insensitive. Content-Type: multipart/form-data; Boundary=xyz does not match boundaryRegex (no IgnoreCase ), so the valid body is rejected with 400. A part with Content-Disposition: Form-Data; name="a" fails StartsWith("form-data", Ordinal) and becomes a plain FormEntry , losing its name and filename. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/Post/MultipartFormData.cs ( boundaryRegex() , and the disposition check near line 119) Fix: Add RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant to boundaryRegex() and compare the disposition type with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase .
descriptions.github:5692963773: Content-Type: multipart/form-data ; boundary=x (optional whitespace before ; , allowed by RFC 9110) leaves MimeType as "multipart/form-data " with a trailing space. The DataHandler lookup misses, and the body is stored as RawPostData instead of being parsed as multipart. Handlers that expect MultipartFormData or UrlEncodedData silently get no data. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/HttpPost.cs:40-60 Fix: Trim the media type (and the parameter part) after splitting at ; , before the DataHandler lookup.
descriptions.github:5692963103: On the public SpanStream , Seek(-2, SeekOrigin.End) moves to Length instead of Length - 2 because it uses Math.Max where Math.Min is needed. Setting Position = Length throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException although Stream allows that position. Currently only NetworkReader uses it and never seeks, so only direct users hit this. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/IO/SpanStream.cs:87-100 , MaxLib.WebServer/IO/SpanStream.cs:27-36 Fix: Use Math.Max(0, Math.Min(Length, Length + offset)) for SeekOrigin.End and accept value == Memory.Length in the Position setter.

What we'd like Footnotes rendered the usual way: a small link in the text, the notes at the end, and a link back from each note. descriptions.github:5692957504: Description Nothing checks that the needs: lists in the GitHub Actions workflows match the jobs that exist. ci-ok aggregates needs: [...] by hand: Removing a job and forgetting its entry here is silent. GitHub does not fail a workflow because a needs: entry names a job that does not exist; the aggregate simply stops waiting for it (or the workflow is invalid and only shows up in the run log). No test in the repository reads .github/workflows/ — the suites are PHP only ( tests/Unit , tests/Integration ) — so a mismatch is caught by a human reading the diff, if at all. It bit us while removing the build-piper-musl job ( 26): the job and its needs: entry had to be removed together, in two files, in the same PR. Where to start - .github/workflows/ci.yml ( ci-ok job) and .github/workflows/release.yml ( publish job). - Add a unit test, for example tests/Unit/WorkflowTest.php , that parses…

descriptions.github:5692854913: Some shipments are sent as one consignment made up of several parcels. The integration doesn't track those yet: such a code shows as unknown , and the integration logs a one-shot WARNING starting with Poczta Polska returned a grouped consignment . What would help: if you see that warning, comment here with how many parcels the shipment had and what the Poczta Polska tracking page showed for it, for example whether each parcel had its own status. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5692854548: Every status seen on real parcels so far maps to a canonical status: posted, in transit, customs, out for delivery, a delivery notice, waiting at the post office, returned, delivered and collected. The rarer outcomes have not appeared on a tracked parcel yet, such as a refused or undeliverable item or a delivery attempt that failed for another reason. Some of those are mapped as problem without having been seen live, and anything else shows as unknown . The integration logs a one-shot WARNING starting with Unrecognised Poczta Polska status whenever it meets a status code it doesn't know. That line holds only the status code. What would help: when you see that warning, paste the line into a comment here, together with what the Poczta Polska tracking page or app said about the parcel at that moment. If a parcel shows as problem while the tracking page says something more specific, that is…

descriptions.github:5692051383: On windows-latest , npm test starts and never finishes; runs sat for hours until cancelled. macOS and Linux pass on Node 22 and 24. CI now fails a test that runs longer than 60 seconds ( --test-timeout=60000 ) and a job after 20 minutes, so the next Windows run should name the test that hangs. Likely suspects are tests that start child processes or the local named-pipe bridge and don't close them on Windows. Windows is experimental (see 28), so this doesn't fail the build, but fixing it is the first step to supporting it.

I ran into one small fault and believe I have found the cause, so I wanted to pass it along. Symptom On my home PC (Windows, keyboard plugged directly into the motherboard), the Num Lock, Caps Lock, and Scroll Lock LEDs went dark after roughly 30 to 60 minutes of normal use. The PC had not gone to sleep and the keys kept working. Pressing the lock keys still changed the state in Windows, but the LEDs stayed dark. Unplugging the keyboard, or pressing a key mapped to QK REBOOT, brought them back. The solenoid was off. The fault did not appear on my work computer over a full day. descriptions.github:5691839656: Problem BarChart, PieChart, and Legend support updating their content after construction. However, updates made after calling add to page() do not update the objects stored on that page. The internal group contains the replacement objects, while the page still contains the original objects. Consequently, exporting the page produces a diagram with stale data, labels, or colors. Calling add to page() again is not a reliable workaround: it adds the replacement objects without removing the old content. Reproduction The same behavior was reproduced with: PieChart.update data(): the page retains the original slices and labels. Legend.update mapping(): the page retains the original color boxes and labels. Color updates also use the same rebuild mechanism and therefore have the same underlying problem. Root cause add to page() adds each object from the internal group to the page. When an update…

descriptions.github:5691730227: Problem you're trying to solve Organisations on Google Workspace keep Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files in Google Drive. OfficeAgent can only reach files on a local disk or in SharePoint/OneDrive, so those teams have to copy files out and back by hand. Scope Office files stored in Drive ( .docx , .pptx , .xlsx ) are in scope. descriptions.github:5691531338: Every tweet is sent to the model each time it is seen. The service worker caches verdicts for the session, but the cache is lost when the browser restarts, so tweets that reappear later cost another API call. Idea: persist verdicts in chrome.storage.local , keyed by tweet ID plus a hash of the active filters, strictness and model settings, with an expiry and a size cap. Things to think about: - Invalidate when filters, threshold, model or provider change. - Keep the cache bounded so storage doesn't grow forever. - Don't cache failed calls. - Don't store more tweet text than needed. Storing only the verdict is enough. This is a bigger change than the other open issues. Please comment with your approach before starting. Where to look: the caching code in background.js and the decisions map in content.js .

descriptions.github:5689993370: call() 's typed overload takes returns: type[T] . Literal[...] (and X | None ) are special forms, not types, so mypy and Pyright fall through to the overload that returns Any . doesn't have this gap, because the return annotation is read from the function itself. Possible directions: - PEP 747 TypeForm , imported only under TYPE CHECKING , since thunc can't take a runtime dependency on typing extensions - Extra overloads for the common cases Requirements: any fix has to pass mypy --strict thunc and Pyright, and must not change runtime behaviour. A small file of reveal type / assert type checks would make the result easy to verify.

descriptions.github:5689993072: Right now every call goes to the model, so re-running a script costs the same every time, and tests that use a real model aren't reproducible. Wanted: - Cache: identical calls (same backend, model, system prompt and prompt text) return the stored answer. - Record/replay: record a run's answers, then replay them, for example in CI, failing loudly on any call that wasn't recorded. Open design questions (please discuss here before writing code): - How is it switched on? thunc.configure(cache="...") , an env var, a context manager? - Where does it store answers? A directory of JSON files is easy to diff and commit. - Should a cached answer still be parsed and ensure= -checked? Probably yes. - How does it interact with trace= ? Where: thunc/core.py ( send is the single point every call goes through) and thunc/config.py . It must stay standard-library only.
descriptions.github:5689992935: Allow a Pydantic model as a return type, next to dataclasses: Constraint: thunc's core uses the standard library only, so Pydantic must not become a dependency. Where: thunc/schema.py - describe() : describe the fields, possibly from model json schema() . - validate() : call model validate(value) and turn a ValidationError into a ValueError with a short message. That message is sent back to the model on retry. Tests: offline only, in tests/test schema.py . Pydantic can be a dev-only dependency, or the tests can skip when it isn't installed. Please comment with the approach before opening a large PR.

descriptions.github:5689715095: What The nl pack masks Dutch BTW-ids as vat id . Add the German counterpart to the de pack: the Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer (USt-IdNr). It identifies sole traders, so it can be personal data. Examples: DE136695976 , DE . Format - DE followed by 9 digits; the first digit is never 0 . - Spaces or dots between groups are common ( DE ). - The 9th digit is a check digit (ISO 7064 MOD 11,10): product = 10 ; for each of the first 8 digits, sum = (digit + product) mod 10 , if sum == 0: sum = 10 , product = (2 sum) mod 11 . The check digit is (11 - product) mod 10 . Spec: BZSt: Aufbau der USt-IdNr. Watch out for - Require an uppercase DE and a non-word boundary before it, so words and identifiers that end in de are not touched. - Look at how nl vat detector handles the NL format in all three backends and keep the structure parallel. Category Reuse vat id , so no new type is needed. Where…

descriptions.github:5689712228: Description BinaryFileResponseStrategy::scheduleFileCleanup() ( src/Http/Response/Strategy/BinaryFileResponseStrategy.php ) sets $connection- onBufferDrain to delete the temp file after the send. For a file of 2 MB or more, Workerman Http::sendStream() ( vendor/workerman/workerman/src/Protocols/Http.php ) replaces onBufferDrain with its own callback and sets it to null at the end. So the cleanup callback is lost, and the file is deleted only when the connection closes (the onClose fallback). On a keep-alive connection the temp file can stay on disk for a long time. This was found while working on issue 899 (PR 950). It is not tested yet. descriptions.github:5689712052: Description The timeout sweeper in src/Worker/ServerWorker.php (around line 141) calls $connection- close() on a connection that stopped. In Workerman 5.2.2, close() with a non-empty send buffer only sets STATUS CLOSING and stops reading ( vendor/workerman/workerman/src/Connection/TcpConnection.php:985-991 ). If the client never reads, destroy() is never called. The socket, the send buffer and the file handle from Http::sendStream() stay open until the worker stops. This is an old problem. It was seen in review of PR 950 (issue 899). A slow-reader client can use it to hold sockets and file handles. descriptions.github:5689427317: Problem Description In lib/state.js , writeJsonAtomic performs a write to a temporary file followed by fs.renameSync(temporaryPath, filePath) . On Windows, background file indexing services, antivirus scanners, or active IDE file watchers (like VS Code) can hold a transient read lock on filePath for a few milliseconds, occasionally causing fs.renameSync to throw an EPERM or EBUSY error. Expected Behavior Atomic writes should be resilient to momentary Windows file locks by attempting up to 3 retries with a small backoff before throwing. Proposed Solution & Implementation Hints In lib/state.js : Relevant Files - lib/state.js - tests/test-flow.js Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Atomic writes retry gracefully on transient Windows locks. - [ ] Existing atomic persistence unit tests continue to pass.

descriptions.github:5689404678: pkg/owasp/vector.go:97 sets IntrusionDetection: 9 - vul . On OWASP's scale not logged is 9, meaning higher likelihood. At ta=7, vul=6, tech=bus=7 the published score is 6.5 x 7 = 45.5 , while recomputing the 8-factor mean from the published vector gives 51/8 = 6.125 , so 42.875 . Existing tests in tests/test retrieval and graph.py and tests/test research mode.py show how parts of the graph are already exercised.

It should read any needed emails or keys from repository secrets, skip providers whose secrets are missing, and report failures without blocking pull requests. Notes Keep request volume low to respect rate limits and polite-pool rules (see .env.example ).

descriptions.github:5687850514: A claim → evidence → paper chain is built only for sentences the writer LLM tagged with [EV: ] , and only in four sections. Optionally flag untagged sentences that contain numbers, comparisons, or citations so the writer or the reviewer sees them. Notes - Tag instructions are in backend/app/agents/research mode/writing.py ; the tag-to-claim conversion is claims linker node . - Do not claim full coverage anywhere in the UI or docs. descriptions.github:5687850317: Claims are extracted per sentence. A sentence with two clauses and one citation counts as a single claim, so the second clause is never checked on its own. What to build Split compound sentences into clause-level claims before they are linked to evidence, for example on semicolons and coordinating conjunctions, while keeping the citation attached to the clause it belongs to. A simple rule-based splitter is fine as a first version. Notes - The claims manifest is built in claims linker node in backend/app/agents/research mode/writing.py . - Claim IDs are deterministic ( {section} cl001 ). Splitting must keep them stable and unique. - Add tests with multi-clause sentences, abbreviations ("et al.", "e.g."), and decimals, which must not trigger a split.
descriptions.github:5687850114: validate citations in text in backend/app/agents/research mode/validation.py resolves an in-text citation by matching only the first-author surname and the year against the corpus. Problem - Two papers by the same first author in the same year are indistinguishable. - Surnames with particles, hyphens, or diacritics (de la Cruz, Müller/Mueller) can fail to match. - A wrong citation that happens to share a surname and year counts as resolved. What to build A stricter match, for example adding the second author or title tokens when available, handling a / b year suffixes, and normalising diacritics. Keep the current behaviour as the fallback so existing reports do not regress. Acceptance - New unit tests cover same-author-same-year ambiguity, diacritics, and suffixes. - Existing validation tests still pass.

descriptions.github:5687586450: Account mode logs in with an SMS code and then keeps itself signed in by refreshing its tokens. The whole flow — requesting the code, exchanging it, refreshing, and listing deliveries — was reconstructed from how the Airmee app behaves, and has never been run against the live service from here. Specifically unconfirmed: - The exact country code format accepted when requesting the SMS (what you type is sent as-is — +46 , 46 and 0046 have not been compared). - The shape of the refresh response, and whether both tokens really rotate. - The shape of the deliveries list. What would help: if setup fails or you get signed out unexpectedly, the warning line from the log plus a diagnostics export. The log line is written to be safe to paste.

descriptions.github:5687584349: Make your first open source contribution! Never contributed to open source before? Start here. Add yourself to the OSS Cameroon contributors page by creating one small file. - You only need a GitHub account - Everything happens on the GitHub website, so you don't need to install anything or use the command line - It takes about 5 minutes This issue is open to everyone. You don't need to ask to be assigned or comment "can I work on this?". Just follow the steps below. Steps 1. Go to the contributors page, type your GitHub username and click Add me .
