Timestamps are currently accepted only as Unix seconds in a plausible range; anything else is refused with a one-shot warning rather than guessed at. descriptions.github:5687583859: Airmee's order object carries its status in two places: a machine-readable code per timeline event, and a human-readable text field. The integration prefers the code, and only falls back to mapping the text when the code is absent — the text is localized and ambiguous, so the fallback deliberately maps only unmistakable wordings. Which of the two the tracking-link route actually returns has never been seen on a real response. The account route is expected to carry both. What would help: if you track a real parcel by tracking link, a diagnostics export would show whether the per-event status code comes through. If it only ever returns the text, the fallback map needs widening and this gets reprioritised.

descriptions.github:5687540452: The Structural Health Monitoring section has six entries and all of them are modal analysis tools (operational or experimental modal analysis and camera based displacement measurement). The section note already says it is thin. The concrete gaps are: - Damage detection and anomaly detection on vibration or strain data. - Sensor data pipelines : acquisition, cleaning and storage of long term monitoring data. - Benchmark datasets from instrumented bridges or buildings, which would also fit Open Datasets. - Fatigue and remaining life assessment tools. Projects must meet the usual criteria: open source license, documentation and either active maintenance or a clear reason to list them anyway. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.
descriptions.github:5687540276: Crack and surface defect detection is one of the most common uses of machine learning in civil engineering, and the AI and Machine Learning section currently has no project for it. The two entries that used to cover it, DeepCrack and crack segmentation, were removed in 10 because neither repository has a license, and DeepCrack restricts its data to non commercial use. SDNET2018 in Open Datasets provides images, but there is no listed model or training code. What is needed A project for crack or defect segmentation or detection on concrete, asphalt or steel surfaces that: - has an explicit open source license for the code, - states the license or terms of any bundled dataset or weights, - documents how to run inference or training. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.
descriptions.github:5687540106: The Learning Resources section covers GIS, geotechnical engineering, hydraulics and general engineering computation, but has nothing for three areas the list itself is strong in: - Earthquake engineering : course notes or worked notebooks on response spectra, ground motion processing, hazard or nonlinear time history analysis. - Structural dynamics : open textbooks or notebooks on single and multi degree of freedom systems and modal analysis. - BIM and IFC : tutorials for IfcOpenShell, openBIM workflows or IFC data handling. Candidates that were looked at and rejected because the repository has no license: the DOLFINx tutorial and seismo-live. A resource needs an explicit open license (code or content, for example MIT or CC BY) and enough documentation to follow without the lecture it was written for. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.

CursorParser survives this (it retries through ("utf-8", "utf-16", "latin-1") ), but ClaudeCodeParser , CodexParser , OpenCodeParser and HermesParser all open with the default UTF-8 and let the decode error escape. descriptions.github:5685537359: Public-mode keys are shared today in person, as a pairing text or a QR code (spec section 9). That works between people who meet, but an organisation (a bank, a newsroom, a public figure) needs a way for anyone to find its key. The spec marks this TBD . Candidates to compare: - A well-known HTTPS path on the organisation's domain ( /.well-known/voxtrust ), like security.txt . - A DNS TXT record, possibly with DNSSEC. - Key transparency logs, so a swapped key is visible. - Reusing an existing system (C2PA trust lists, WebFinger, Keybase-style proofs). What matters: a verifier must be able to tell a key that rotated legitimately from one an attacker swapped, and the answer must work offline after the first lookup. Comments with prior art and trade-offs are very welcome before any spec text is written.
descriptions.github:5685536907: C2PA Content Credentials are becoming the standard for signed media provenance. File mode is close to it in spirit (a signed manifest inside the file), and a bridge would let C2PA-aware tools show a Vox Trust seal (roadmap, phase 6). Open questions, a design note answering them is a great first contribution: - Should the VOXT manifest become a custom C2PA assertion, or should Vox Trust per-chunk digests map onto C2PA's existing hashing of media? - C2PA signs with X.509 certificates; Vox Trust uses bare Ed25519 keys pinned by contacts. How do the two trust models coexist? - What does a verifier show when the C2PA signature and the Vox Trust seal disagree? Prototype with the c2pa Rust crate. Please start with a short design note (a markdown file in docs/decisions/ ) before a large PR.
descriptions.github:5685536454: The demo, the README and the website exist in English, Portuguese, Spanish, Simplified Chinese and Arabic. descriptions.github:5685536145: The core already implements the pairing text of spec section 9 ( vox trust core::pairing , with encode and decode ), but the command-line tool cannot produce or read one. Today you share a public key as 64 hex characters. Proposal: - vox-trust pubkey KEYFILE --pairing [LABEL] prints voxtrust:0:public: < 64 hex [: ] . - vox-trust verify FILE --pin also accepts a pairing text (or a file containing one) besides a bare hex key. - Circle pairing texts contain the secret, so the CLI must never print one unless asked explicitly, and the help text should say why. Where: crates/vox-trust-cli/src/main.rs (argument parsing and the USAGE text), tests in crates/vox-trust-cli/tests/ . Keep the existing exit codes. A CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] is welcome.
descriptions.github:5685535666: Vox Trust is meant to be built into apps that already record or send voice: messengers, voicemail, podcast and newsroom tools, support platforms. descriptions.github:5685535295: Only the author has reviewed the design and the code. Before anyone relies on it, it needs eyes from people who break protocols for a living. Scope, most valuable first: 1. Threat model: attackers or attacks that are missing, and claims that are too strong. 2. File mode (spec section 6): domain separation, what the signature covers and what it does not ( byte rate , extra chunks, chunk order), replay, downgrade between circle and public mode. 3. crates/vox-trust-core (about 2 000 lines, no unsafe ): the WAV parser and the manifest decoding. 4. crates/vox-trust-cli/src/keyfile.rs : Argon2id parameters and XChaCha20-Poly1305 usage. Findings that could hurt users go through private vulnerability reporting (SECURITY.md); everything else as issues. Reviewers will be credited in the changelog and the threat model.
descriptions.github:5685534877: The specification becomes 1.0 only after a second implementation, written by someone other than the author, agrees with the reference on every test vector (roadmap). descriptions.github:5684982544: Summary With hooks.transparent prefixes = ["sudo", "sudo -E"] , rtk discover counts sudo RTK DISABLED=1 docker ps and RTK DISABLED=1 sudo docker ps as bypasses ( 3808), but not the same lines with an expanded value: rtk rewrite "sudo docker ps" rewrites under that config, so dropping the assignment would recover the savings. Cause strip disabled prefix for analytics ( src/discover/registry.rs ) walks raw lexer::tokenize tokens, which split one shell word at $ : RTK DISABLED=$CI is two tokens, RTK DISABLED= and $CI . The walk treats $CI as the command word, finds it unsupported, and falls back to strip disabled prefix , which does not peel sudo . Walking coalesced words ( lexer::coalesce words , as without rtk disabled in src/discover/mod.rs does) would keep the assignment whole. A missed count, not a wrong one: develop does not count these lines either. Related: 3756, 3808.

descriptions.github:5684207074: What is wrong run.( Engine).Submit checks ActiveRunForLock and then calls CreateRun as two separate statements. The index on runs.lock key is not unique, so two submits that land between those calls both succeed. That can happen with two UI requests, or the CLI in one terminal and the UI in another. Two runs then hold one lock, which is exactly what ADR-0004 exists to prevent. What we want Make the check and the insert one atomic statement, so it also holds across processes: Report zero rows affected as the LockConflictError . The alternative is a partial unique index on lock key WHERE status IN (…) AND lock key != '' , which needs a migration. Where to look - src/internal/run/engine.go ( Submit ) - src/internal/store/runs.go ( CreateRun , ActiveRunForLock ) - src/internal/store/migrations/ if you take the index route Definition of done - [ ] A test submits the same lock key…
descriptions.github:5684206511: What is wrong labctl never installs a signal handler, so cmd.Context() is context.Background() and Ctrl-C kills the process with Go's default action. Scripts started through internal/toolchain run in their own process group ( Setpgid ), so the terminal's SIGINT does not reach them. They keep running with no parent, and their run stays running until the next engine start reconciles it. That breaks the promise in ADR-0003. Two smaller effects of the same gap: - labctl ui exits without calling Shutdown on the HTTP server. - scenario verify --watch sleeps with time.Sleep , which no context can interrupt. What we want - In cli.Execute , run the root command under signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) via rootCmd.ExecuteContext . Everything already reads cmd.Context() , so cancellation flows to run.Engine and each process group gets its graceful SIGTERM. - labctl ui calls…
descriptions.github:5684205957: What is wrong Engine.Get returns the Scenario held in the engine's cache, but only after setting s.Active on it. Any two goroutines that call Get at the same time, or one that calls Get while a run reads the scenario, race on that field. - go test -race ./internal/service/scenario/ reports it on main in TestActivate ConflictsPerScenario , which fails most runs. - The race is also live in labctl ui , because its HTTP handlers call Get concurrently. What we want Stop writing to the cached value. Return a shallow copy with Active filled in, so every caller stays the same. descriptions.github:5684142376: The README says to put RiffPlayer behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS when exposing it to the internet, but gives no examples — that's where many people get stuck. What to do: create docs/REVERSE PROXY.md with working, copy-pasteable examples for at least Caddy (simplest, automatic HTTPS) and nginx ; Traefik is optional. Link it from the note in the README. Acceptance criteria - [ ] You actually tried the examples (with a real domain, or localhost + a self-signed cert) and noted which versions you used. - [ ] Settings that matter for audio streaming (large bodies / long timeouts / buffering), if any, are mentioned.
descriptions.github:5684142179: Problem A: In Admin → Users → "Change pw", leaving the field empty and pressing Save sends the request. The server silently ignores an empty password ( if (password) ), but the UI closes the editor as if it had been saved. Problem B: If creating a user fails, the message is shown as Error: Username already taken — with the "Error:" prefix ( String(createMut.error) ). Other pages (Wrapped, Discover) strip the prefix. Where: web/src/pages/admin/UsersPage.tsx What to do: (A) disable Save while the password field is empty (or don't submit). (B) strip the prefix or use error.message . Acceptance criteria - [ ] Two new tests in UsersPage.test.tsx : Save is disabled / no request for an empty password; the error message is shown without the prefix.
descriptions.github:5684141991: A few actions swallow errors and show nothing, so the user presses a button and nothing seems to happen. Where - web/src/components/PlaylistCard.tsx — Play: catch { // ignore } - web/src/components/home/ContinueListeningSection.tsx — "Jump back in": catch { // ignore … } - web/src/components/StarButton.tsx — silently reverts the star when the request fails What to do: on failure show a short, clear message through useToastStore (e.g. "Couldn't start playback"). Don't change the existing behaviour (optimistic revert etc.). Acceptance criteria - [ ] All three places show a toast on failure. - [ ] Each has a test that makes the API reject and asserts the toast message.
descriptions.github:5684141770: When a library scan can't be started, Admin → Libraries shows the browser's blocking alert() . Everywhere else the app uses the toast for transient messages. Where: web/src/pages/admin/LibrariesPage.tsx (around line 31: alert(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to start scan') ). Toast store: web/src/store/toast.ts — useToastStore.getState().show('message') . Acceptance criteria - [ ] No alert() left; the error appears in the Toast component. - [ ] LibrariesPage.test.tsx is updated: instead of spying on window.alert , assert the message in the toast store.
descriptions.github:5684141489: Follow-up to the player bar issue: other icon-only buttons also rely on title alone. descriptions.github:5684141276: The icon-only buttons in the player bar (Shuffle, Previous, Play/Pause, Next, Repeat, More options, Lyrics, …) only carry a title="…" . title is not a reliable accessible name for screen readers. descriptions.github:5683888258: Reproduction On current main , fetch the spec the server serves and look for $ref s that point at schemas it doesn't define: Expected Every $ref in /openapi.json resolves. Actual GET /v1/sessions/{session id}/stream declares its text/event-stream response as $ref: /components/schemas/ServerStreamEvent , but the live document never defines ServerStreamEvent . Only scripts/dump openapi.py adds it, when writing the committed openapi.json , so the checked-in file is fine and the served one isn't. descriptions.github:5683511344: Problem or use case There is no omni command that closes or deletes a session. The API supports it ( DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} ), and the web UI can archive. From a terminal, the closest is omni host stop-session . That stops the runner but leaves the session in the list. A script or a user cleaning up test or probe sessions must call the HTTP API by hand, with a bearer token. Proposed solution omni session close ... (archive) and omni session delete ... (with a confirm, or --yes ). Both should take --server and use the same auth as omni session export . Alternatives considered curl -X DELETE with a token from the server's auth flow. It works, but it is undiscoverable and makes users handle tokens themselves. Related: 4834 and 7498 (the agent-side sys session close gaps).

How many devices will this feature impact? Unknown What are your project timelines? Flexible Additional context The interplay between ACL and the object deletion APIs have been frustrating for at least 2 customers. If you have the same (or similar) feature request, please upvote this issue with thumbs up 👍 and use the comments section to provide answers to the questions above.

descriptions.github:5682904874: Debugging a live indexing run means grepping stack traces. Structured logs with a correlation id per request make failures traceable end to end. descriptions.github:5681673047: Summary Only SIGQUIT is handled. SIGTERM and SIGINT use the default action, so the process dies at once and leaves the pid file behind. nginx does a fast shutdown on TERM/INT: it closes connections and deletes the pid file. Repro pid logs/r.pid; , start, kill -TERM . - nginx: exits 0, pid file removed. - ruxen: killed by the signal (exit status 143), logs/r.pid left behind. nginx reference src/os/unix/ngx process.c:55-58 (terminate signal); src/os/unix/ngx process cycle.c:660 ( ngx delete pidfile ). Unlocks — Notes Same flag plumbing as SIGQUIT, with no drain. Where in ruxen src/main.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See CONTRIBUTING.md; comment here before starting so two people don't do the same work.
descriptions.github:5681672067: Summary All three directives are ignored, so Set-Cookie from the upstream is passed through unchanged. Repro The upstream sends Set-Cookie: a=b; domain= path=/old/; Secure . Config: proxy cookie domain example.com; proxy cookie path /old/ /new/; proxy cookie flags a httponly samesite=strict nosecure; . - nginx: domain=example.com; path=/new/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict , without Secure . - ruxen: unchanged. nginx reference ngx http proxy module.c:2699 (cookie rewrite), :4564 (flags). Unlocks proxy cookie.t (1–8) and proxy cookie flags.t (1–7, 9–10, 12–14). Both files then pass. Notes It is a response-header rewrite on the proxy path only; supports variables and regex ( / ). It can be split into three PRs, one per directive. Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 .
descriptions.github:5681671532: Summary proxy method is accepted and ignored, so the upstream always sees the client's method. Repro location /m { proxy method POST; proxy pass } with an upstream that echoes $request method , then curl /m . - nginx: upstream sees POST . - ruxen: upstream sees GET . nginx reference src/http/modules/ngx http proxy module.c:439 (directive), :1236 ( ngx http proxy create request ). Unlocks proxy method.t (2–4; the file then passes). Notes It is a complex value (variables allowed) and inherits from the parent. Render it into the request line in run location handler . Take it off IGNORED STMT in the same PR. Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See CONTRIBUTING.md; comment here before starting so two people don't do the same work.
descriptions.github:5681671059: Summary types {} is swallowed and default type is ignored. MIME types come from a hardcoded 18-entry table that appends ; charset=utf-8 to text types, and unknown extensions get application/octet-stream . nginx uses the configured types map ( include mime.types in practice), falls back to default type (default text/plain ), and adds no charset unless charset is set. Repro Request /a.foo , /noext and /index.html . - nginx: text/x-foo , text/x-default , text/html . - ruxen: application/octet-stream , application/octet-stream , text/html; charset=utf-8 . nginx reference src/http/ngx http core module.c:311,319 (directives), :3660 (built-in default types), ngx http set content type . Unlocks — Notes Build a per-location HashMap at prepare time; the hot path does one lowercase-extension lookup, as now. Re-measure m3 and static 8k . Keeping the charset suffix would need charset support. Where…
descriptions.github:5681670291: Summary ssl protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; is a hard error ( insecure version rejected: TLSv1 ). That exact line is in common distro default nginx.conf files, so unmodified configs don't load. rustls can't speak TLS 1.0/1.1 anyway. Repro http { ssl protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ... } , then ruxen -t . - nginx: ok. - ruxen: [emerg] bad value for ssl protocols (insecure version rejected): TLSv1 . nginx reference src/http/modules/ngx http ssl module.c ( ssl protocols bitmask). Unlocks ssl sni reneg.t gets past config load. Its renegotiation subtests then fail by design in rustls, so it won't fully pass. Notes Keep TLSv1.2/1.3 from the list and log [warn] TLSv1, TLSv1.1 are not supported and ignored . A list with only old versions should still be [emerg] . Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See…

descriptions.github:5681669368: Summary There are three separate reason-phrase tables, and any code they don't list becomes OK : return 413 sends HTTP/1.1 413 OK , and the same goes for 307/308/406/414/416/429/504. 503 says Service Unavailable , where nginx says Service Temporarily Unavailable . nginx sends NNN with an empty reason for codes it doesn't know (205, 418, 599). Repro location = /413 { return 413; } (likewise 307, 504, 418), then curl -si . - nginx: 413 Request Entity Too Large , 307 Temporary Redirect , 504 Gateway Time-out , 418 . - ruxen: 413 OK , 307 OK , 504 OK , 418 OK . - client max body size overflow also answers 413 OK . nginx reference src/http/ngx http header filter module.c:58+ ( ngx http status lines[] ). Unlocks — Notes One const table indexed like nginx's, used by all three call sites. For 418/599, nginx also sends no body and no Content-Type. Where in ruxen src/http.rs , src/file.rs…

The compare device picker ( c ) polls every 250 ms and does follow a resize. descriptions.github:5681659150: What happens writeFd loops until every byte is written, but it returns early, without an error, when write returns 0. The caller sees success while the rest of the frame was dropped. wire.zig treats the same case as an error. Where - tools/zzzbench/tty.zig:39-46 - tools/zzzbench/wire.zig:303-316 ( writeWireBytes returns error.ProbeGone when n == 0 ) Suggested fix Return an error when n == 0 instead of returning normally. A real file descriptor does not return 0 for a non-empty write, so move the loop into a function that takes the write call as a parameter, and test it with a stub that returns 0. tty.zig has no tests today, so register it in tools/zzzbench/tests.zig .

None of them are used. The only caller, model catalog.inspect , uses init , deinit and .data , and GGUF parsing happens in gguf metadata.zig with its own cursor. - model catalog.inspect takes a gpa and throws it away with = gpa; . Where - tools/zzzbench/peer.zig:66-69 - shared/mmap reader.zig:31-115 - tools/zzzbench/model catalog.zig:139-149 Suggested fix 1. Delete canRunEngine . 2. Cut MmapReader down to init , deinit and data , or replace it with a small map/unmap function. 3. Drop the gpa parameter and update the one call. Neither module is exported, so nothing outside the repository is affected. To test, run zig build check and zig build test . If a file is removed, tools/tidy.zig reports any import left pointing at it.

descriptions.github:5681561743: Why The Appearance dialog draws clickable controls, but its keyboard handling currently only supports Escape. Scope Add a visible focus indicator and Tab/Shift+Tab traversal for existing controls. Enter/Space activates the focused action; Escape closes and restores composer focus. Reuse the current appearance actions and limits; this does not depend on a separate disabled-button change. Done when - Theme, text size, UI scale, reading width, Reset, and Done are reachable without a mouse. - Focus remains within the dialog and cannot trigger underlying send/navigation actions. - Values still clamp at existing limits; clicks and keys agree even if all adjustment controls remain present. - Focus is visible in both themes, survives redraw/resize, and never changes the composer draft. Starting points controls, appearance actions, settings keyboard branch.
descriptions.github:5681560876: Why The header/footer show a project basename, which is ambiguous when two folders have the same name and cannot be copied directly. Scope Add a clearly labelled Copy path control next to the header project breadcrumb. Copy the complete current canonical project path using the existing SDL clipboard pattern. Do not change the active folder or add a new global shortcut. Done when - Same-basename projects copy their distinct full paths. - Spaces, Unicode, and long paths copy without the display label's truncation. - During a pending chat switch, copy the project shown by the breadcrumb. - Clipboard failure is reported; clicking does not alter the draft, caret, or chat selection. Starting points displayed project breadcrumb, clipboard pattern.
descriptions.github:5681560437: Why Clearing a library query currently requires editing the text; there is no clear control. Reuse the existing action/target system. Done when - Clicking clears the query, returns to the first page, and keeps input focus. - A prior in-flight query cannot replace the new empty-query results. - The button never edits the chat draft or activates a selected result. - Empty queries hide the control; IME composition is cancelled cleanly before clearing. descriptions.github:5681559956: Why The chat library uses the same No matches status for an empty workspace, empty archives, and a query with no results. Done when - Empty Search explains creating/importing a chat; empty Archives explains archiving. - Empty Import Pi explains that there are no importable results in configured Pi storage, without claiming no sessions exist. - A nonempty query says no matches and suggests changing/clearing it. - Searching, indexing, incomplete sources, and errors retain their status rather than being mislabeled as empty. Starting points library scope and status.
descriptions.github:5681559500: Why Text size, scale, and reading width already clamp their values, but their minus/plus buttons still look and behave as enabled at the limits. Scope Render the exhausted direction as disabled and omit its hit target. Keep existing limits: text 12–24 px, UI scale 75–175%, and width 560–1120 px. Reuse the palette and existing adjustment actions. Done when - Each minimum disables only minus; each maximum disables only plus. - Disabled clicks do not change values, enqueue saves, or invalidate layouts. - Moving back into range re-enables the button; Reset restores the normal state. - Disabled controls remain recognizable in dark and light themes. Starting points value clamps, adjustment drawing.

Starting points thinking overlay, existing action, keyboard branch.
descriptions.github:5681558836: Why Shortcuts are implemented and listed in CLI help, but there is no in-app reference. Scope Add a Shortcuts entry in the sidebar opening a read-only help dialog. descriptions.github:5681551856: 赏金平台 / Platform GitHub 原始链接 / Source URL 漏洞描述 / Description [Bounty $1,000] FP32 ttnn.cumsum returns NaN after infinity or overflow 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete…

descriptions.github:5681232002: 🤖 This issue was found and written with AI (Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5). Problem --clear-session doesn't actually clear the session. In main.py the browser context is created first, and aenter loads storage state.json into it. Only after that does session.clear session() delete the file: The run still uses the old cookies, and aexit writes them back to disk. So the flag is a no-op. Fix - Delete the file before creating the context, e.g. by passing a fresh=True option to BrowserSession or by deleting it in main.py before the async with . - Alternatively, call context.clear cookies() like --form-login does. - Add a test asserting the context is created with storage state=None when --clear-session is given.

descriptions.github:5680992241: GroqClient.SystemPrompt hard-codes English: The model handles many languages perfectly well. The only reason the review is English-only is that the prompt says so. What to build The flag should substitute the target language into the prompt and translate the section headings to match, so the output reads naturally rather than as translated English headings over a non-English body. Why it matters This project was built for the developer with no team to ask. That developer is not necessarily an English speaker, and a review you have to translate before you can act on it is a review you will skip. Notes - Default stays English, so nothing changes for existing users. - Accept ISO 639-1 codes ( pt , es , fr , de , ja ) and fall back to English with a warning on stderr for anything unrecognised. - Nothing parses the section names, so they are free to translate.
descriptions.github:5680986143: The CLI reviews local changes ( git diff , --staged , --diff ). It cannot review a pull request that is not checked out locally. What to build GitHub serves the raw diff for any PR at .diff , so this can be a plain HTTP GET followed by the existing review path — no API client, and no authentication needed for public repositories. Why it matters It turns the tool from "review what I am about to commit" into "review what someone sent me", which is the other half of reviewing alone: the maintainer triaging a drive-by contribution with nobody to ask for a second opinion. Notes - Private repositories need a token; treat that as a follow-up, not part of this. - Large PRs will hit the existing 60k-character truncation. That is fine, but the warning should name the PR that was truncated. - Parsing the URL belongs in CliOptions ; fetching belongs in its own small type next to GitDiff .

So a client cannot display "this will cost approximately X" before the user commits. The user sees only…

descriptions.github:5680942128: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Support/KeychainStore.swift:25-39 : setKey first calls SecItemDelete , then return SecItemAdd(...) == errSecSuccess . The method is marked , and every caller ignores the result: - Settings/AI/APIKeySetupView.swift:148 (sets result = .valid right after) - Settings/BrainSettingsView.swift:282 - Settings/ConnectionsSettingsView.swift:125 Scenario The user replaces a working key. SecItemAdd fails (the keychain is locked or access is denied). By then the old key has already been deleted and the new one wasn't saved, yet the UI shows "valid / connected". The next chat fails with an authentication error, far from the real cause. Suggested fix - Update the item with SecItemUpdate , falling back to SecItemAdd , so the old key is never deleted first. - Check the result at each call site (or make setKey throw the OSStatus ) and show an error instead of .valid .
descriptions.github:5680936876: Problem Sources/MomoMCP/MCPClient.swift:56-70 : LineBuffer.append keeps appending data until it sees \n , with no size limit. Both ProcessTransport and UnixSocketTransport use it. The server side already caps its buffer at 16 MB ( MCPSocketServer.swift:191 ); the client side has no cap. Scenario A buggy third-party MCP server streams a huge response, or endless output without a newline. Momo's memory grows until macOS kills the app. Suggested fix - Cap LineBuffer at 16 MB, matching the server. - On overflow, finish the stream with an error and close the transport.
descriptions.github:5680936294: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Context/MCPConnections.swift:66-77 starts the server process with ProcessTransport . If client.connect() throws (for example ClientError.timedOut after the fixed 30 s in MCPClient.swift:149 ) or listTools() throws, the catch block only sets .failed . It never calls client.close() , which is the only path that terminates the process ( MCPClient.swift:49-52 ). clients[id] stays nil , so the next refresh() starts yet another process. Scenario A server configured as npx -y some-server takes more than 30 s to install on first run. Momo marks it failed, but the node process keeps running. Every settings change or refresh adds another orphaned process. Suggested fix - Call await client.close() (or terminate the transport) in the catch . - Make the initialize timeout longer than, or separate from, the per-call timeout.

GIFs have no audio, so leave out the opus flags. Keep Arg::VideoChain(&TRANSCODE CHAIN) so --fps and --resize still work, and register it next to the gif - mp4 line in insert media family . descriptions.github:5680591943: Description cli/mesi-cli.go never closes the HTTP response body. In URL mode the body is fetched at client.Do(req) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:306 ) and read with io.ReadAll(content.Body) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:317 ), but there is no defer content.Body.Close() anywhere, so the http.Response is dropped unread on every path that leaves the URL branch. Impact today is small but real: - the body is read to EOF on the success path, so the connection is handed back to the pool anyway and main returns immediately afterwards; - on every error branch os.Exit(1) is called, and os.Exit runs no deferred functions, so a defer content.Body.Close() placed at the top of the branch would not fire there either — the fds are only reclaimed when the process dies. So no leak is observable from the CLI as it is used today. The defect is the missing Close() itself: it is invisible only because the process is short-lived…

descriptions.github:5680543331: Why this is useful JSON currently uses two-space indentation, which is pleasant for manual review. In pipelines that immediately parse the result, whitespace adds bytes without adding information. A compact serialization option could reduce artifact size while preserving all records and existing field semantics. Scope Discuss an explicit JSON-only compact mode using standard-library serialization. Keep pretty-printed JSON as the default unless a separate compatibility decision is made. Scope Propose a plain-text layout for the existing Failure fields and agree whether it shares the Markdown budget option or has a separate clearly named limit. descriptions.github:5680539332: Why this is useful The Markdown header currently reports one total for all unique failure records. Scope Prototype an opt-in summary-first renderer that budgets concise identities before adding detailed blocks. Keep the current ordered-prefix strategy available. descriptions.github:5680538142: Why this is useful Character slicing uses Python code points, which is the documented budget unit, but a visible character can contain several code points. descriptions.github:5680536950: Why this is useful The CLI excerpts failure messages and details, but suite, class, test name, and source fields can still be very long. descriptions.github:5680535390: Why this is useful A reader currently sees replacement markers but cannot distinguish how many recognized matches were removed, or which broad rule families were involved. descriptions.github:5680534881: Why this is useful Failure traces and report paths can reveal a developer username through paths such as /home/demo-person/project/test.py or C:\Users\DemoPerson\project\test.py . Scope Design an explicit privacy option that masks configured home-directory prefixes in every visible failure field, without discovering arbitrary personal files or rewriting paths by default. Acceptance criteria - Cover synthetic POSIX and Windows prefixes, separators, case policy, and paths containing spaces. - Use path-boundary-aware replacement so a short prefix cannot corrupt unrelated filenames or prose. - Preserve enough…
descriptions.github:5680534411: Why this is useful A failure may contain a JSON fragment represented as escaped text, such as {\"password\":\"demo-value\"} where the backslashes are literal characters in the displayed diagnostic. The current redactor operates on the displayed text; it is not an arbitrary decoder. Recursively decoding every field would risk changing useful evidence and creating unpredictable runtime costs. Contributors could first define whether one layer of JSON string escaping warrants support; ordinary unescaped JSON assignments are already handled by the current matcher. Scope Focus on one layer of JSON string escaping around a secret assignment. Demonstrate a synthetic missed pattern and design a single bounded normalization or matching step. Do not add recursive decoding, base64 decoding, or URL handling; URL query values belong to the separate query-redaction proposal. Acceptance criteria…
descriptions.github:5680533963: Why this is useful The assignment matcher accepts identifier names containing words such as TOKEN or SECRET anywhere in the key. Harmless diagnostics such as token count=17 or secret length=12 are therefore candidates for masking even when the numbers explain the failing assertion. Relaxing this behavior blindly could expose real credentials, so the useful contribution is a small policy change supported by both sensitive and harmless synthetic examples. Scope Discuss a conservative key-boundary or narrow exception policy. Target diagnostic counters rather than introducing a general disable-redaction switch. Acceptance criteria - Provide before/after examples showing the lost debugging information and the intended supported exception. - Include credential names with prefixes, suffixes, hyphens, quotes, and varied case as negative controls. - Keep genuine credential assignments masked and…
descriptions.github:5680533430: Why this is useful A project-specific account number, internal host, or invented credential may not match any built-in heuristic. Users currently cannot supply exact values they already know should disappear. An explicitly selected local literal list could complement the heuristics without adding a regex language or sending report content to another service. This should remain optional because treating broad strings as secrets can destroy useful diagnostic context. Scope Design a small literal-redaction input contract, including encoding, maximum file size, minimum entry length, ordering, and error behavior. Do not scan the environment or home directory automatically. Acceptance criteria - Agree on a CLI interface and ensure no file is read unless the user selects it. - Use bounded literal matching and define overlapping, duplicate, blank, and Unicode entry behavior. - Ensure errors…
descriptions.github:5680532921: Why this is useful Provider prefixes and assignment patterns do not cover a private key represented as a multiline PEM block in failure details. Matching a single line would leave the remaining synthetic payload visible. The project already warns that redaction is incomplete; a narrowly defined block matcher could address a recognizable format without implying that every kind of key material is detected. Scope Evaluate matching explicit private-key BEGIN/END markers as whole blocks. Define behavior for malformed or unmatched markers before writing the implementation. Acceptance criteria - Construct fake marker names and payloads at runtime; never commit a real or usable private key. - Cover RSA, EC, encrypted, and generic private-key labels within the agreed supported set. - Keep public certificates and ordinary prose unchanged unless an explicitly documented rule applies. - Bound…
descriptions.github:5680532397: Why this is useful The current redactor handles bearer credentials and key-like assignments, but a failure containing Authorization: Basic DEMO VALUE or Cookie: session=demo-value; theme=dark has different structure. HTTP debugging output can appear inside failure details even though captured stdout is excluded. A grouped header policy would be easier to review and maintain than unrelated expressions for individual authentication providers. Scope Agree on supported Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie forms and whether cookie values should all be hidden. Keep this limited to recognizable header lines. Acceptance criteria - Use synthetic header values and include multiple headers, mixed case, whitespace, and harmless non-header counterexamples. - Preserve the header name and unrelated neighboring lines while hiding the selected sensitive value. - Ensure multiline…
descriptions.github:5680531939: Why this is useful URLs in assertion messages can contain access credentials as query values. The current assignment expression can match names such as access token , but its unquoted value rule does not recognize ampersands as query boundaries. A synthetic example such as can therefore lose useful neighboring information. Other credential parameter names require an explicit policy rather than indiscriminately masking every query value. Scope Design a bounded URL-query redaction pass for a small documented set of credential keys; preserve useful URL structure without fetching or following any URL. Acceptance criteria - Add synthetic cases for first, middle, repeated, blank, and percent-encoded sensitive query parameters. - Preserve harmless parameters, delimiters, and fragments exactly where the chosen contract permits. - Keep replacement idempotent and cover both standalone URLs and…
descriptions.github:5680531426: Why this would help Reports may be consumed while another process is still writing them. The bounded read already handles growth beyond the byte ceiling, but a same-size rewrite or replacement can produce an inconsistent snapshot without necessarily violating that limit. Proposed scope Investigate best-effort detection of report changes during reading using file-descriptor metadata before and after the read. State the limits of detection rather than promising a filesystem lock or a perfect snapshot. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Reproduce relevant change cases deterministically with instrumented reads or controlled writer synchronization. - Define which detectable changes cause a ReportError and ensure no partial brief is emitted. - Keep byte limits…
descriptions.github:5680530879: Why this would help Argparse permits unambiguous long-option abbreviations by default. A script using a shortened option can break or change interpretation as the CLI grows, even though the documented full option has not changed. Proposed scope Consider disabling implicit long-option abbreviation while retaining intentional short aliases such as -o. Agree on the compatibility impact for users who already rely on abbreviated flags. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Show the current acceptance of an unambiguous abbreviated option and record the proposed new error behavior. - Require full documented long names while keeping all existing explicit aliases operational. - Keep argument errors on stderr with the established usage-error exit status. - Cover…
descriptions.github:5680530317: Why this would help Many command-line tools accept a dash as the output destination, allowing a script to substitute either a filename or standard output in one variable. This CLI currently treats that value as a literal file path. Proposed scope Consider reserving --output - for stdout and document how to create a file literally named dash when needed. This is an ergonomic proposal, so confirm the compatibility decision before changing path handling. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Route --output - through the normal stdout branch without creating a dash-named file. - Preserve ordinary --output atomic file writing and input/output collision protection. - Define a literal filename escape such as ./- and verify it remains usable. - Cover both output formats…
descriptions.github:5680529844: Why this would help Exact failures across reports currently collapse into one record with the first source. This is convenient for concise briefs, but it hides whether the same failure occurred in several shards or attempts and cannot be disabled by library callers. Proposed scope Design an explicit deduplication policy, considering global exact matching, per-report matching, and disabled deduplication. Treat optional occurrence counts and source provenance as part of the same coherent model decision. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Keep current global exact behavior as the default unless a versioned compatibility change is agreed. - Define whether repeated input paths count as new occurrences and distinguish outcome multiplicity from report multiplicity…
descriptions.github:5680529313: Why this would help JUnit testcase time attributes can help a caller recognize expensive failures or timeouts. The current model drops that information, so library users cannot inspect reported durations without a separate XML pass. Proposed scope Propose an optional duration field with a precise representation and a clear invalid-value policy. Keep duration extraction separate from any sorting, prioritization, or new default rendering behavior. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Define the expected unit and representation, including whether the original decimal spelling is retained. - Cover zero, fractional seconds, absent values, invalid text, negative values, and non-finite numbers. - Decide whether duration participates in deduplication; explain behavior…
descriptions.github:5680528779: Why this would help A build script may need to check that reports are readable supported JUnit XML before another step consumes them. Running the current converter also constructs and writes a failure brief even when that output is unwanted. Proposed scope Design an explicit validation-only mode that runs the supported input checks without producing Markdown or JSON. Define whether test failures affect its exit status separately from malformed reports. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Reject incompatible rendering and output flags with an actionable argument error. - Validate every supplied report and specify whether diagnostics stop at the first error or aggregate multiple errors. - Keep valid reports containing test failures distinguishable from invalid XML…
descriptions.github:5680528266: Why this would help Atomic output uses NamedTemporaryFile followed by os.replace. On systems with file modes, the replacement inherits the temporary file permissions rather than necessarily retaining those of an existing destination, which matters in shared workspaces. Proposed scope Document and, if needed, implement an explicit permission policy for new and replaced output files. Treat preserving restrictive permissions as part of the design rather than copying every filesystem attribute. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Demonstrate current new-file and replacement modes on POSIX with a controlled umask. - Agree whether existing destination permissions are preserved or intentionally reset and explain the tradeoff. - Avoid broadening permissions…
descriptions.github:5680527771: Why this would help The current --output option intentionally replaces an existing file atomically. In scripted runs, users may want accidental destination reuse to fail so an earlier useful brief is not overwritten. Proposed scope Propose an opt-in no-clobber output mode with a documented concurrency guarantee. Preserve the current replacement default unless maintainers agree to a separate breaking change. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Reject an existing destination without modifying its contents and report a clear nonzero status. - Avoid a check-then-replace race that can overwrite a file created by another process between those operations. - Specify symlink and unsupported-filesystem behavior, including a safe failure when the guarantee cannot be met…
descriptions.github:5680527199: Why this would help Users may pipe a brief into head or another consumer that exits before reading everything. BrokenPipeError can arise during stdout writing or final buffering, and generic input-error handling does not describe that situation well. Proposed scope Agree on a quiet, platform-aware broken-pipe policy for the CLI and implement it at the output boundary. Keep genuine output-file failures distinct from an intentionally closed pipe. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Reproduce an early-closing consumer with a sufficiently large output and observe the real process exit status. - Avoid interpreter-shutdown tracebacks or repeated stderr diagnostics after a broken pipe. - Specify whether the exit status follows a conventional signal status or a…
descriptions.github:5680526677: Why this would help A user may press Ctrl-C while processing a large batch or writing a brief. KeyboardInterrupt is not currently part of the CLI error handling, and cancellation behavior has no focused coverage. Proposed scope Define a predictable interrupt contract at the command boundary, including exit status, concise stderr behavior, and temporary-output cleanup. Avoid swallowing interrupts inside the reusable parser. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Simulate cancellation during report reading and during output writing without depending on interactive timing. - Return the agreed interrupt status without a Python traceback from the command-line entry point. - Keep an existing output file intact when cancellation occurs before its atomic replacement…
descriptions.github:5680526138: Why this would help ReportError currently provides a human-readable message only. Integrators must parse that message to distinguish unreadable files, unsupported encoding, invalid XML, and unsupported roots or to display an XML line and column. Proposed scope Propose stable optional error attributes such as category, source, and XML position while preserving ValueError compatibility and useful existing text. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Define a small documented category set that does not depend on platform-specific OSError wording. - Preserve exception chaining and the current CLI exit code for invalid inputs. - Expose parser positions only when available; do not add raw XML snippets to exceptions. - Cover representative I/O, encoding, syntax, root, and…
descriptions.github:5680525581: Why this would help The reader currently retains raw bytes, decoded XML, the full ElementTree, and extracted failures during conversion. Reports with many passing tests may incur substantial memory cost even though most nodes are discarded from the final result. Proposed scope Create a reproducible standard-library benchmark and evaluate an incremental parsing prototype. This is an investigation; replacement of the parser depends on demonstrated benefit and semantic parity. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Measure elapsed time and peak Python allocations for passing-heavy, failing-heavy, nested, and duplicate-heavy synthetic inputs. - Compare extracted failures and order against the current implementation on representative fixtures. - Preserve encoding…
descriptions.github:5680525040: Why this would help Deep suites are intentionally handled without recursive Python traversal, but depth and element count remain unbounded within the file-size ceiling. Highly nested or broad XML can spend resources without providing useful failure context. Proposed scope Investigate optional maximum XML depth and element-count limits with measured examples. Agree on acceptable compatibility limits before changing parsing behavior. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Measure a deeply nested report and a wide report with many non-outcome elements under the existing byte ceiling. - If limits are accepted, enforce them during parsing rather than only after allocating the complete tree. - Preserve DTD/entity rejection, UTF-8 restrictions, and atomic failure…
descriptions.github:5680524489: Why this would help A relatively small XML file can contain many compact failure elements. The byte limit does not directly bound the size of the Failure list or the work spent deduplicating large batches of tiny outcomes. Proposed scope Propose an optional parser outcome budget with explicit raw-versus-unique counting. Exceeding a resource limit should be an input error, not silent omission presented as complete results. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Define whether the limit counts every failure/error element or only unique retained failures, and explain the resource tradeoff. - Cover exact-boundary batches, repeated outcomes, and the limit crossing between two input files. - Keep the existing no-partial-output behavior and useful limit diagnostics…
descriptions.github:5680523987: Why this would help The parser has an inclusive per-file byte limit, but an arbitrary number of individually valid reports can still consume substantial time and memory in one invocation. A batch-wide limit would help callers bound that work. Proposed scope Add an optional aggregate byte budget to the parsing contract and, if agreed, expose it through the CLI. Count actual bytes read rather than trusting only filesystem metadata. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Specify the default, inclusive boundary, and interaction with the existing per-file limit. - Cover many small reports that exceed the total while each remains under the individual limit. - Avoid returning partial failures or replacing an existing output when the budget is exceeded. - Define how…
descriptions.github:5680523447: Why this would help The current parser rejects a report that declares failures but contains no extractable outcomes anywhere. A failure in one sibling suite can still satisfy that report-wide check while another suite declares missing failures. Proposed scope Design an optional strict counter-validation mode that compares suite declarations with their relevant descendants. Establish semantics for aggregate parent counters before considering a stricter default. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. descriptions.github:5680523418: Feature Factory Simulation & Abstraction What to Solve? Binary Factorium must run on extremely limited hardware ( ), and thus cannot naively use a tiled simulation or the conventional model. The constrains together make it hard to solve easily. What should the simulator essentially contain or do ideally? It should: - Update O(1) when nothing changes - Update O(n) or O(log(n)) when changes happen (with n = parts to update ) - Not hang when numerous updates happen in a short period of time (also in long periods ideally) - Consume a fixed amount of RAM at any point. - Possibly be asynchronous. - Be Binary-Spectacular ;) I am not an expert in this field ;-; (\ unlike what most factory games with large/infinite world target, Binary Factorium's primary targets are the Fri3d Badges)
descriptions.github:5680522889: Why this would help The parser uses the nearest named suite and supports inherited names. Proposed scope Propose preserving a structured suite path in addition to the existing display suite. Decide how named and unnamed testsuite/testsuites containers contribute before changing deduplication. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Cover two parents whose same-named child suites contain otherwise identical test failures. - Keep the current nearest-name behavior available for callers that rely on the suite field. - Define unnamed-container and namespace behavior without delimiter-based identity collisions…
descriptions.github:5680522348: Why this would help Some JUnit reports identify the source file and line on each testcase. Proposed scope Design optional source-location fields for testcase file and line attributes. Keep the report source distinct from the test source, and agree on missing, malformed, and platform-specific values. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Read location attributes without opening source files or checking whether the reported path exists. - Define line-number validation and whether invalid metadata is ignored, preserved, or reported. - Keep older Failure constructors compatible and explicitly decide whether location affects…
descriptions.github:5680521822: Why this would help The parser currently uses the failure message when present and falls back to the type attribute otherwise. A report containing both loses its exception type, which can distinguish an assertion failure from a timeout with similarly worded messages. Proposed scope Propose an optional, backward-compatible model field for the original failure/error type, independent of message fallback. Coordinate any serialized-field change with the output contract. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Preserve both attributes when they are present and retain useful fallback behavior when either is missing. - Define whether differing types make otherwise identical outcomes distinct for deduplication. - Keep existing positional Failure constructors valid if a new…
descriptions.github:5680521227: Why this would help A combined report can contain failures from many packages, while a developer may be investigating one suite or only infrastructure errors. Today the command always includes every unique failure before applying output limits. Proposed scope Design optional selectors for outcome kind and test identity, covering suite, classname, and test name in a single contract. Decide matching rules and their effect on --fail-on-failures together. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. Acceptance criteria - Specify exact or wildcard matching, multiple-selector composition, and case sensitivity. - Keep report validation independent of selection so an excluded invalid report cannot masquerade as success. - Define whether the failure exit flag checks selected outcomes or all parsed…
descriptions.github:5680520666: Why this would help Failure deduplication currently happens after each report has been read and parsed. Supplying the same report repeatedly therefore repeats I/O and XML work even though the resulting failures keep only their first source. Proposed scope Consider deduplicating identical input file references before parsing, with an explicit policy for relative paths, absolute paths, and symbolic links. Preserve the spelling of the first accepted source. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. descriptions.github:5680519620: Why this would help Shell wildcard expansion differs between Bash, PowerShell, and Windows command prompts. Proposed scope Design explicit repeatable include and exclude pattern options, expanded by the application against a chosen base directory. Treat include and exclusion semantics as one coherent feature. Discuss CLI/API contract before implementation. This is a proposal, not a confirmed defect or a promise that the interface will be accepted. descriptions.github:5679932145: The cheapest entry left in the ratchet. Array.prototype.sort() sorts in place , so it mutates the array it was given; toSorted() returns a new one. Why this one is worth doing properly rather than mechanically Two of the three production call sites are in data-table.component.ts , which sorts rows it was handed through an input() . Sorting those in place mutates the caller's array — a signal's value, in most cases — which is how a table can reorder data a parent component still believes it owns, without the parent's signal ever being set. Swapping to toSorted() is the fix, but each site is worth a glance to see whether anything downstream was relying on the mutation. Note toSorted() needs a reasonably current runtime target; it is available in the browsers this project targets and in the Node used for specs. descriptions.github:5678907905: 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete when all of the following are satisfied: - FP32 ttnn.cumsum preserves IEEE/PyTorch behavior after +inf . - FP32 ttnn.cumsum…

descriptions.github:5677602459: cmd dmesg is a stub. Kernel logs go to serial (and the boot framebuffer early on) but there is no buffer userspace can read back, or if there is one it is not wired to a syscall. First step is checking what DEBUG in src/kernel/debug.h actually emits and whether a ring buffer exists. If not, add a small one behind the existing log path, then an extended syscall that snapshots it out under a lock, then make dmesg print it. Worth deciding what release builds do since most logging is debug only.
descriptions.github:5677600372: cmd lspci in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp prints a stub line. PCI enumeration happens at boot in src/drivers/bus/pci/ but userspace never sees the device list. Needs a new extended syscall (297 or wherever the numbering is by then) that fills an array of small descriptors (bus, slot, function, vendor id, device id, class code) and returns the total count, same shape as SYS INPUT ENUM DEVICES. Then the builtin just prints the table. include/uapi/input.h plus the input enum case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp are the reference for the uapi side.
descriptions.github:5677599797: There is no netstat. The TCP and UDP tables live in src/net/tcp.cpp and src/net/udp.cpp but nothing exports counts to userspace (sockets in use, per state, rx/tx bytes). Simplest version is a small extended syscall filling a struct with tcp and udp socket counts per state, next free number is 297. sys net status in src/net/net.cpp is the pattern to copy, and the input enum devices case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp shows the array-plus-count shape. Then a netstat builtin in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp that prints it. The socket tables are plain arrays so ktesting the counters is easy.
descriptions.github:5677599522: Every UDP socket has one 1500 byte receive slot with overwrite semantics (src/net/udp.cpp). If two datagrams land before the app calls recvfrom the first one is gone, and nothing reports it either. Turning the slot into a small ring, 4 entries or so, would fix the common case. The receive handoff runs inside net poll() under the table spinlock so the write path has to stay cheap, a memcpy into a preallocated ring is fine. Some way to see overflow would be good too, a debug warn or a dropped counter.
descriptions.github:5677599224: Every resolve goes out on the wire even when we just resolved the same name. dns resolve() in src/net/dns.cpp already retries three times with fresh transaction ids, there is just no cache anywhere. A small table of the last few answers with a short TTL (30-60 seconds is plenty for this stack) would do. The resolver runs from syscall context so keep it under the existing locks. A ktest for expiry and eviction can go next to the dns tests in src/net/dns tests.cpp.

When a column has a non-text type (e.g. UUID), passing '' produces a runtime SQL error. Steps to reproduce 1. Define a model with a UUID primary key and a nullable UUID foreign key, e.g.: 2. Create a row without setting parent id . The column is stored as NULL. 3. Load the row (Model::where("id = '...'").first()) . queryMap reads the NULL as an empty string and stores attributes["parent id"] = "" . 4. Modify any other field and call save() . UPDATE fails: In Model::save() , the attribute-collection loop does not skip empty values: Because NULL columns are read back as "", the UPDATE statement always includes them, and PostgreSQL rejects '' for non-text types. Fix Skip empty values before adding them to the…

Tmux treats the leading = as an exact-match marker and resolves those targets as lit ; if that session is absent, the lookup can fail. One possible approach: Cover literal-only, plain-only and both-present cases, including distinct window indexes; the target rule is defined in tmux 3.6a. descriptions.github:5676783179: Description Follow-up from 64 / PR 255 (review finding). src/BinaryDownloader.php ( download() , the curl setopt array() call): the return value is ignored. If cURL rejects one option, the remaining ones are skipped silently, so the HTTPS-only and redirect limits could be missing without any error. Also curlOptions() is protected static and called with static:: , so a subclass can override the security settings. Where to start Throw DownloadException::downloadFailed($url, ...) when curl setopt array() returns false; call self::curlOptions() or make it private. Definition of done - A failing option aborts the download with a DownloadException. - Test covers it; CHANGELOG entry if behaviour changes.

descriptions.github:5676728882: Why Some searches expand a tree of decisions one ply at a time: a game, a plan, a sequence of tool calls. The full tree does not fit, and there is no stored graph. Monte Carlo tree search keeps the branches it has tried, picks the next one with an upper confidence bound, and backs a score up the path. 133 covers finding a path through a successor function. This issue is the tree of sampled decisions on top of that idea. Proposed API In a new package search : Options: - WithIterations(n int) , default 100. - WithExploration(c float64) , default math.Sqrt2 . This is the UCB1 constant. - WithRand(r rand.Rand) . When nil, each rollout picks a uniform legal action with crypto/rand . A non-nil source makes the search reproducible. Behavior - A nil actions , next , or score returns an error. - WithIterations below 1 returns an error. - Selection walks from the root by UCB1 until it reaches a…
descriptions.github:5676728489: Why Nearest-neighbor search for retrieval keeps a stack of graphs. The top layer is sparse. The bottom layer contains every point. A search starts at the top, greedily walks to a closer neighbor, then drops a layer. That is the HNSW search. The points stay in the caller's table. The graph stores ids, because a vector is not a comparable label in any useful way. This issue is the layered graph and the greedy search. It is not a database. There is no index file, no metadata filter, and no delete. Proposed API A new package nn : Behavior - distance must be zero or positive. A negative distance returns an error at search or insert time. - m and efConstruction below 1 return an error from New . A nil distance returns an error. - k or ef below 1 returns an error from Search . - Insert of an id that is already present does nothing and returns nil. - The neighbor sets are chosen by the HNSW…
descriptions.github:5676728256: Why Some DAGs accept a vertex only after several successful samples, and only after its parents are accepted. Avalanche counts confidence that way. The sample itself is a network call. The library can own the counter and the parent rule. The caller owns the query. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - sample , beta , or rounds below 1 returns an error. A nil query returns an error. - Parents are incoming neighbors. - A vertex with no parents may be accepted on its own run of successes. - A failed query resets that vertex's consecutive count to 0. It does not reset other vertices. - The result is in GetAllVertices order, and contains only accepted vertices. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers. - The function does not open a connection, pick peers, or sign anything. query is the whole…
descriptions.github:5676728025: Why A block DAG is not a chain. One way to order it is to paint a well-connected subset blue and leave the rest red. A set is a k-cluster when every member has at most k other members that it cannot reach and that cannot reach it. The largest such set is expensive to find. The greedy coloring used by GHOSTDAG walks in topological order and adds a vertex to the blue set when the blue anticone is still within k. This is that coloring. It is not a node, and it does not choose a block for a peer to mine on. HeaviestBranch is the walk on a tree. This is the coloring on a DAG. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - k below 0 returns dag.ErrInvalidK . - Two vertices are incomparable when neither can reach the other. - The walk order is the stable topological order, the same one TopologySort returns. - A…
descriptions.github:5676727781: Why Some DAGs decide that event A has seen event B only when the paths between them cover a supermajority of authors. Hashgraph calls this strongly seeing. The predicate is ancestor counting. Virtual voting and witness election stay with the caller. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected . - members below 1 returns an error. A nil author returns an error. - Missing from or to: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Seeing is reachability along directed edges, including a vertex seeing itself. - The threshold is strictly greater than 2 members/3 . For 4 members the threshold is more than 8/3, so 3 authors. The test should use that case. - Authors are compared with == . The function does not check that every author id is one of a fixed set. An author outside the expected set still counts as one distinct author, which can only make the count…
descriptions.github:5676727518: Why Fork choice on a tree of blocks walks from the root and, at each block, follows the child whose subtree carries the most weight. GHOST and LMD-GHOST are that walk. The weight is whatever the caller counts: work, stake, or the latest vote of each validator. The library does not know which. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected . - A vertex with two incoming edges, or a vertex not reachable from root, returns dag.ErrNotTree . - A cycle returns gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - Subtree weight is the vertex's own weight plus the subtree weights of its children. A vertex is not counted twice. - Ties break by GetAllVertices order of the children. - The returned path starts at root and ends at a leaf. Vertices are the graph's own pointers. - Negative weights are allowed. They only change which child wins. - Missing root…
descriptions.github:5676727251: Why Max flow ( 193) asks how much can move. Some networks also have a price on each edge. Splitting a payment across channels is the usual case: send a given amount, stay inside each edge's capacity, and pay the least fee. Proposed API In flow , beside MaxFlow : Successive shortest paths with potentials. Costs may be negative. A negative cycle in the residual graph returns flow.ErrNegativeCycle . Behavior - amount below 0 returns an error. amount of 0 returns a shipment of value 0 and cost 0. - A negative capacity returns flow.ErrNegativeCapacity . - Missing source or sink: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Directed edges carry flow in their direction. An undirected edge shares its capacity across the two directions, and that capacity is not doubled. - For every vertex other than source and sink, flow in equals flow out. - Flow on an edge stays inside its capacity. - Among shipments of…
descriptions.github:5676726980: Why Clustering merges labels into groups as pairs arrive: two addresses that shared an input, two records that are the same entity. Building a graph first is an extra copy. Disjoint sets answer "are these the same group" in nearly constant time. Proposed API A new package unionfind : Union by rank and path compression. Behavior - Connected on a label that was never seen is false. - Union of a label with itself adds it and leaves it in a group of one. - Representatives are deterministic for a given sequence of calls. - Groups does not return a representative that the caller has to interpret. It returns the members. - The package does not know about graphs. A caller with a graph passes labels. Tests - Five unions that form two groups. Connected matches. Groups matches, in insertion order. - Path compression does not change Connected results. - Find on an unknown label returns false…
descriptions.github:5676726745: Why Some DAGs are ordered by a score that includes the ancestors, not by the vertex alone. A transaction pool ranks a transaction by the total fee of itself and everything that must come before it, divided by the total size of that same set. StableTopologySort can compare vertices, and it cannot see that sum. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - The set for a vertex is itself plus every vertex that can reach it. - The key is the sum of num over that set, divided by the sum of den over that set. - A denominator sum of 0 returns dag.ErrZeroDenominator . - Ties break by GetAllVertices order. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers, one per vertex in the graph. - Empty graph: nil, nil. - This is a ranking, not a topological order. A later vertex can rank ahead of an ancestor. Callers who need a…
descriptions.github:5676726508: Why Callers often need the best few items, not a full ordering. A mempool keeps the highest-paying transactions. A ranking keeps the top vertices by score. Retrieval keeps the nearest matches. A full sort does more work than that, and it allocates a second copy of the whole list. Proposed API In util : Behavior - k below 0 returns util.ErrInvalidK . k of 0 returns an empty slice and a nil error. - A nil better returns an error. - A nil or empty items returns an empty slice. - The result is a new slice. items is left as it was. - Equal items keep their original order. - Running time is linear in the length of items times log of k , using a heap of size k . The doc comment says so. A caller who wants a nucleus-style prefix computes it from this ordered prefix. The function does not grow a sampling API. Tests - Ten integers, k of 3, the three largest in order. - Ties: two equal best items…
descriptions.github:5676726283: Why AStar ( 185) keeps every unsettled vertex in a heap. When the frontier is large, the memory is the problem. Iterative deepening A repeats a depth-first search with a rising limit on the estimated total cost, and stores only the current path. Planners use it when the graph of states does not fit in memory. Proposed API In path , with the same cost and heuristic contract as AStar : Behavior - Costs must be zero or positive. A negative cost returns path.ErrNegativeWeight . - The search raises the limit to the smallest f-value that was beyond the previous limit. - It returns a cheapest path when the heuristic is admissible. The doc comment says so. It does not check the heuristic. - Missing vertices, an unreachable goal, and start equal to goal follow AStar . - Ties break by vertex and edge order. - The doc comment says AStar is the better choice when the frontier fits in memory…
descriptions.github:5676725921: Why On a graph that branches widely, keeping every partial path is too expensive. Beam search keeps a fixed number of them and drops the rest. Decoders use it to keep a few partial sequences. The same bound keeps a path search inside a memory limit. The result can miss the cheapest path. That is the trade. Proposed API In path : Behavior - width below 1 returns path.ErrInvalidWidth . - Partial paths are simple. A vertex is not repeated on one path. - At each step the search keeps the width partial paths with the best score. descriptions.github:5676725632: Why A route from one vertex to one other vertex does not need a distance for every vertex. Proposed API In path , beside AStar ( 185): Behavior - Directed graphs: the backward search walks incoming edges. Undirected graphs: either direction. - Missing start or goal: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - Unreachable: path.ErrUnreachable . - start equals goal: a one-vertex path and cost 0. - A negative cost: path.ErrNegativeWeight . - The path vertices are the graph's own pointers, start first and goal last. - Ties break by the order vertices and edges were added. - The two searches stop once the cheapest meeting point is settled. descriptions.github:5673427734: Current behavior 🐛 BorderVisual (Skia) replaces its RectangleClip objects whenever the border or corner radius geometry changes, but never disposes the old ones. In UpdatePathsAndCornerClip() , the old childClipCausedByCornerRadius and backgroundClip are just set to null and new clips are created (L203-L212, L330-L346). Since 24230, RectangleClip caches one geometry (a native SKPath ) and only releases it in DisposeInternal() (RectangleClip.skia.cs L42). Nothing calls Dispose() on a replaced clip, so its cached path is freed only by the SKPath finalizer when the GC gets around to it, not deterministically. Impact is low: it is bounded to one path per replaced clip and the finalizer does clean it up eventually. It can only pile up between GCs, for example while a rounded Border is being resized or animated frame after frame. This was confirmed by code inspection on master (7a2214115d5)…
